sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, I also hope the Government will also provide a complementary set of policies, including childcare leave based on number of children, introducing paid caregiving leave and upgrading Flexible Work Arrangements guidelines to enforceable legislation.

sections.label: Space for younger generation
sections.summary: The passage calls for giving younger Singaporeans space to explore and suggests piloting a 10-year through-train programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is why we should give the younger generation more space to explore and grow, stimulating their imagination and sense of purpose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I suggest further reducing emphasis on examinations, such as by piloting a 10-year through-train programme from primary to secondary school, allowing students to choose whether to take the PSLE.

sections.label: AI reliance and workload
sections.summary: AI accelerated tasks, raised speed expectations, deepened reliance, expanded work scope and increased work density and volume.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The adoption of AI tools did not reduce workload.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: AI accelerated tasks, which raised the expectation for speed, which deepened reliance on AI, which expanded the scope of work, which further increased the density and volume of work for each employee.

sections.label: Burn-out economic cost
sections.summary: Burn-out costs the Singapore economy an estimated $15.7 billion annually in lost productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Burn-out costs the Singapore economy an estimated $15.7 billion annually in lost productivity.

sections.label: Singapore TFR decline
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR has plunged below one, holding steady at 0.97 since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our TFR has since plunged below one, holding steady at 0.97 since 2023.

sections.label: Family support policy proposals
sections.summary: Speaker will propose per child childcare leave, paid caregiving leave and enforceable flexible work arrangement policies at the Committee of Supply debate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Such financial measures matter and we also need a supplementary set of policies to complement them, focused on giving Singaporeans back the time and energy to actually build a family and parent with presence, patience and joy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is why at the upcoming Committee of Supply debate, I will be putting forward proposals on per child childcare leave, paid caregiving leave and having actual enforceable flexible work arrangement policies rather than guidelines.

sections.label: Private tuition spending rise
sections.summary: Singaporean families spent $1.8 billion on private tuition in 2023, up 64% from a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singaporean families collectively spent $1.8 billion on private tuition in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is up 64% from a decade ago.

sections.label: Assessment as diagnostic tool
sections.summary: Assessment should be a diagnostic tool to track a child's progress, identify learning needs and celebrate growth rather than grade and sort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Rather than competitive grading and sorting, we should use it as a diagnostic tool to track a child's progress over time, identify specific learning needs and celebrate their growth.

sections.label: Workforce qualities and new board
sections.summary: Speaker hopes the new Statutory Board from merging WSG and SSG builds career development frameworks and ensures labour protection and skill certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It reflects the very qualities we say we want in our workforce – adaptability, entrepreneurial thinking and a willingness to take calculated risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I look forward to hearing more about the mandate of the new Statutory Board formed by the merger of WSG and SSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope it will build complementary and updated frameworks for career development and ensure labour protection and skill certification to accommodate diverse work arrangements, while safeguarding longer-term income security and career progression.

sections.label: Economic growth and headwinds
sections.summary: The economy grew 5% last year, but projected growth of 2% to 4% this year shows external headwinds are real and likely to persist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, our economy grew by 5%, which gives us confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But this year's projected growth of 2% to 4% reminds us that external headwinds are real and likely to persist.

sections.label: Retirement and senior employment measures
sections.summary: CPF top-ups, higher contribution rates, the Long-Term Care Support Fund, Senior Employment Credit and a Tripartite Workgroup support retirement adequacy and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates strengthen retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Long-Term Care Support Fund reinforces CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Senior Employment Credit and the Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment encourage businesses to continue hiring and retaining older workers.

sections.label: AI principles reflected in Budget 2026
sections.summary: The speaker's three Budget 2024 AI principles appear reflected in Budget 2026's National AI Council, AI Missions and enterprise incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the Budget 2024 debate, I proposed three principles: first, AI strategy must be driven from the centre with direct oversight from the Prime Minister; second, we should focus on high value, sector-specific deployments, at scale; and third, that trust and governance will be our differentiator in a world racing ahead with AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am encouraged to see these principles reflected in Budget 2026: in the National AI Council chaired by the Prime Minister; in the AI Missions across advanced manufacturing, connectivity, healthcare and finance; and in the stronger enterprise incentives including the Champions of AI and SME grants, and the emphasis on deeper AI literacy, governance and responsible deployment.

sections.label: Agentic AI value creation share
sections.summary: The speaker's firm estimates Agentic AI will double its share of AI-driven value creation from 17% to 29% by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2028, my firm estimates that Agentic AI will double its share of AI-driven value creation, from 17% today to 29%, outpacing traditional AI and GenAI.

sections.label: AI Missions as innovation engines
sections.summary: AI Missions must be innovation engines and living laboratories for multi-agent systems, safety standards and human-in-the-loop designs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our AI Missions must, therefore, be more than transformation roadmaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They must be innovation engines – living laboratories for multi-agent systems, safety standards and human-in-the-loop designs.

sections.label: AI-managed city as export showroom
sections.summary: A safe, efficient and trusted AI-managed city makes Singapore a living export showroom, generating intellectual property, productivity gains and exportable capability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we can demonstrate an AI-managed city that is safe, efficient and trusted, Singapore becomes a living export showroom.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They are sector-wide operating systems – generating intellectual property, productivity gains and exportable capability.

sections.label: Multi-year support for AI Champions
sections.summary: Support and financial backing for Champions of AI must be structured and multi-year, tied to measurable productivity outcomes and CEO and Board accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we expect our Champions of AI to redesign operating models over multiple years, then support and financial backing must also be structured and multi-year, tied to measurable productivity outcomes and anchored by accountable leadership at the chief executive officer (CEO) and Board level.

sections.label: Teaching Singaporeans to think with AI
sections.summary: Singaporeans must learn to think with, challenge and govern AI, requiring investments in mid-career reskilling, certifications, mentorship and applied learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, we must teach Singaporeans not just how to use AI but how to think with AI, to challenge it and to govern it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This means serious investments in mid-career reskilling and professional certifications in AI supervision and AI operations, mentorship and applied learning and building a culture of collaboration with AI.

sections.label: AI literacy and apprenticeships
sections.summary: Proposes mandatory AI literacy modules, apprenticeships and externships, and curricula covering critical thinking, ethics and domain knowledge for mid-level roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mandatory AI literacy modules across Institutes of Technical Education, polytechnics and universities, structured apprenticeships and externships when they are still in school, when they work directly alongside seasoned professionals and AI systems and curricula that develop critical thinking, problem-solving, functional skills, ethics, systems thinking and domain knowledge necessary to progress quickly into mid-level roles.

sections.label: ComLink+ AI Capability Milestones
sections.summary: Suggests AI Capability Milestones for ComLink+ families, covering parent AI literacy, children's safe AI use and supervised AI tools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, ComLink+ supports families with goals around employment and education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We can introduce AI Capability Milestones, such as when the parent completes foundational AI literacy module; when a child demonstrates safe and effective use of AI for schoolwork; or when a family sets up supervised AI tools for job search or for their home-based business.

sections.label: Tracking AI outcomes and displacement
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will commit to annually releasing AI-attributable value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes alongside jobs displaced data.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As we pursue this agenda, will the Government commit to tracking and releasing annual value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes attributable to AI adoption across key sectors alongside data on jobs displaced by AI?

sections.label: Agentic AI and Singapore's future
sections.summary: States that if done right, agentic AI will not replace Singaporeans, and that orchestration shapes the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we get this right, agentic AI will not replace Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For a small nation, multiplication is not optional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is how we remain sovereign, how we remain competitive, how we remain extraordinary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the age of agentic AI, those who orchestrate will shape the future.

sections.label: National AI Council and missions
sections.summary: Notes the Prime Minister's announcement of a National AI Council and sector-specific AI missions for key economic and social sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister's announcement of the formation of a National AI Council and the launch of sector-specific AI missions signal a clear intent to move toward Government-supported application of AI in sectors that are key to Singapore's economy and society.

sections.label: Data centre efficiency and small AI
sections.summary: Cites the PUE target of 1.25 in IMDA's DC-CFA2 and software-level accountability requiring Government-funded AI solutions to prioritise small, task-specific models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Alongside infrastructure, efficiency standards, like the power usage effectiveness (PUE) target of 1.25 in the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) latest Data Centre – Call for Application (DC-CFA2), which will also require software level accountability ensuring that the AI Solutions receiving Government funding, including those under the enhanced Enterprise Innovation Scheme prioritise small AI and task-specific models that require a fraction of the energy of general purpose large language models (LLMs).

sections.label: Data centre grid reliability gap
sections.summary: Ireland requires data centres to have 100% on-site backup capacity and 80% renewable matching, while Singapore's DC-CFA2 framework only targets 50% green energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While Ireland requires data centres to be active partners in grid reliability through 100% on-site, backup capacity and 80% renewable matching, our current DC-CFA2 framework only targets 50% green energy, leaving a significant gap that our national grid and, by extension, the ordinary taxpayer must bridge.

sections.label: AI energy disclosure regulation
sections.summary: The National AI Council must bridge digital ambition and environmental reality, with a regulatory framework mandating energy disclosures for large-scale AI developers, as the EU will do by August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If we are to achieve our net-zero 2050 commitments, the National AI Council must bridge the gap between digital ambition and environmental reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We need a clear regulatory framework that mandates energy disclosures for large-scale AI developers, like the European Union (EU) which will begin mandating energy disclosures for large AI developers by August this year.

sections.label: National Adaptation Plan question
sections.summary: The speaker asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment about plans to submit a National Adaptation Plan to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Last month, I asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment about our plans to submit a National Adaptation Plan (NAP) to the United Nation's Framework Convention on Climate Change.

sections.label: Just transition fund for workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks what retraining support ExxonMobil's up to 500 retrenched Singapore workers by 2027 receive and calls for a dedicated just transition fund for petrochemical workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In October 2025, ExxonMobil announced it would retrench up to 500 workers in Singapore by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What specific retraining support is being provided to these hundreds of workers affected by such structural shifts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If we can find $500 million to finance regional green infrastructure via the Financing Asia's Transition Partnership fund, I am sure we can also find the resources to ensure no Singaporean worker is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I call for the establishment of a dedicated just transition fund to assist, not just the 500 workers laid off, but to help all workers in the petrochemical industry in the coming years who may be affected as we transition away from fossil fuels, including providing specific guidance in transiting to different industry or jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Prime Minister announced in his Budget speech that Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebates have now been lowered by 45% across the board and the maximum rebate has been reduced from $60,000 to $30,000.

sections.label: Heavy vehicles zero emissions incentive
sections.summary: The $40,000 Heavy Vehicles Zero Emissions Scheme incentive launched 1 January 2026 may remain under-utilised without faster hydrogen pilots or permanent battery swap licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the $40,000 incentive under the Heavy Vehicles Zero Emissions Scheme, launched on 1 January 2026 may remain under-utilised unless we can move faster on shortlisted hydrogen pilots or permanent battery swap licences to support our delivery community and logistics sector.

sections.label: Subsidy gap for complex dental cases
sections.summary: Despite higher subsidies and MediSave use for tooth saving treatments, the subsidy gap for complex cases must be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the higher subsidies and MediSave use for tooth saving treatments, we must address the subsidy gap for complex cases.

sections.label: Dental subsidies and IP riders
sections.summary: A senior was denied PG or CHAS dental subsidies, prompting a call to harmonise subsidies, while from April 2026 new IP riders will not cover deductibles and co-payment caps rise $6,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: But she was denied PG or CHAS subsidies for the procedure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to harmonise these subsidies so that our seniors are not financially, penalised because their dental-related medical needs require a hospital setting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: From April 2026, new Integrated Plan (IP) riders will no longer cover deductibles and co-payment caps will rise $6,000.

sections.label: CPF premiums and Basic Healthcare Sum
sections.summary: Higher monthly payouts do not address lump sum annual insurance premiums, so the CPF Board is asked to let members who meet the Basic Healthcare Sum retain excess funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While this boosts monthly payout, it does not help with the lump sum nature of annual insurance premiums which can reach several thousand dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Therefore, will the CPF Board consider allowing CPF members who have me their Basic Healthcare Sum to retain a portion of excess funds in their Ordinary Account or a dedicated insurance sub-account.

sections.label: Green data centres and Small AI
sections.summary: Efficiency gains may be offset by rebound effects, so enterprise innovation grants should encourage energy-efficient, task-specific Small AI models instead of large general-purpose models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Although the Government has launched a Green Data Centre Roadmap and set energy saving targets, if overall usage continues to expand, the so-called efficiency improvements may very well be offset by rebound effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Therefore, in terms of enterprise innovation grants, we should encourage the development of more energy-efficient, "Small AI" and task-specific models rather than uniformly using large general-purpose models across the board.

sections.label: Support amid global uncertainties
sections.summary: Steps have been taken to support Singaporeans through global uncertainties while investing in long-term economic resilience and social well-being.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Important steps have been taken to support Singaporeans through ongoing global uncertainties while continuing to invest in our long-term economic resilience and social well-being.

sections.label: Four areas and disability support
sections.summary: Four areas are considered: persons with disabilities and caregivers, vulnerable young children, youth development, and families with complex needs, welcoming Budget support including the Long-Term Care Support Fund top-up and DAC expansion.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I will consider this across four areas: firstly, persons with disabilities and their caregivers; secondly, vulnerable young children; thirdly, youth development and fourthly, families navigating complex needs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the continued support in this Budget for persons with disabilities and their caregivers, including the top-up to the Long-Term Care Support Fund and the planned expansion of Day Activity Centre (DAC) capacity.

sections.label: Preschool affordability and access
sections.summary: The Budget continues to strengthen affordability and access to the preschool sector, steps aimed at ensuring no child is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget continues to strengthen affordability and access to the preschool sector, and these are important steps at ensuring no child is left behind.

sections.label: Youth development Budget investments
sections.summary: This Budget invests in traineeships, skills development and employment pathways for youth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On youth development, this Budget makes important investments in traineeships, skills development and employment pathways.

sections.label: Families and Budget effectiveness
sections.summary: Recent parental leave, housing and healthcare enhancements reduce financial strain and enable family stability, and the Budget's effectiveness lies in enabling Singaporeans to participate and stay connected.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Recent enhancements in parental leave, housing support and healthcare initiatives are significant steps towards reducing financial strain and enabling family stability.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Families often serve as primary coordinators across education, employment, healthcare and community systems, particularly during transitions, such as school-to-work or caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Policies that empower families, not only as recipients of services, but as partners in navigating institutional supports can help sustain participation and reduce discontinuities between transitions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When our investments enable individuals to remain embedded in shared institutions across life stages, they strengthen not only individual outcomes but our collective capacity to act in times of uncertainty and change.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In that sense, the effectiveness of this Budget lies not only in terms of the opportunities it creates but in the extent to which it enables Singaporeans to participate, contribute and remain connected over time.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This way, it lays the foundation for a "we first" society grounded in shared responsibility and common purpose.

sections.label: Survey on daily costs
sections.summary: About 60% of over 1,000 respondents cited daily costs as their top concern and nearly one in five highlighted housing pressures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: About 60% of over 1,000 respondents cited daily costs as their top concern and nearly one in five highlighted housing pressures.

sections.label: Survey on employment challenges
sections.summary: Nearly half of 433 respondents cited lack of career progression as their biggest challenge and more than one in four mentioned underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: On employment, nearly half of 433 respondents cited lack of career progression as their biggest challenge and more than one in four mentioned underemployment.

sections.label: AI training and skills gaps
sections.summary: Over 100,000 Singaporeans took AI-related courses last year, while survey respondents cited unpreparedness, time constraints and weak training-to-job linkages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over 100,000 Singaporeans took AI-related courses last year – a positive sign.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: One in five survey respondents felt unprepared for AI-related shifts in their industry and nearly half said they lacked sufficient training due to time constraints or difficulty finding relevant programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: The focus group's discussions reinforced this, highlighting weak training-to-job linkages and skills mismatches as persistent concerns.

sections.label: Resident co-founds safety initiative
sections.summary: Vareck Ng co-founded a volunteer initiative to improve safety for active mobility users and worked with LTA's Active Mobility Team.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Vareck Ng, a young resident, co-founded a volunteer initiative to improve safety for active mobility users, both walkers and cyclists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Together, we identified problem spots and worked with the Land Transport Authority's (LTA's) Active Mobility Team to improve safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   An ideal budget does not just help us to get through this year but lays the foundation of Singapore's long-term development.

sections.label: Investing in people, Team Singapore
sections.summary: Investing in people so they feel included builds confidence and dedication, which is investing in Singapore's future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: If a society makes its people feel that they are not being left behind, they will be more confident and willing to dedicate themselves to the country.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is what we call "Team Singapore." Investing in people is investing in Singapore's future. : Mr Deputy Speaker, AI can multiply our advantage but only if it strengthens people, not sidelines them.

sections.label: Budget's most important investment
sections.summary: The most important investment in this Budget is not in technology alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: The most important investment in this Budget is not in technology alone.

sections.label: AI reshaping industries and tasks
sections.summary: AI is already reshaping industries and doing repetitive, rule-based, data-heavy work faster and cheaper than humans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: AI is here, AI is not arriving, AI is not five years away, but it is already reshaping industries, changing how some tasks are being done and it is moving faster than most forecasts predicted even three years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: What AI does best today and will get better at doing tomorrow is work that is repetitive, rule-based or data heavy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Machines can now do these tasks faster at lower cost and often with greater consistency than humans and this performance gap will continue to widen and not narrow.

sections.label: Humans controlling AI use
sections.summary: Singapore's job is to keep humans in control of how AI is used, not let it dictate values.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Singapore's job and this includes my job, is to make sure that we as humans remain in control of how AI is used and not let it dictate our values.

sections.label: AI risks and accountability
sections.summary: Accountability means recognising AI risks, regulating disallowed AI content for certain audiences, and ensuring a clear chain of accountability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Accountability also means recognising the risks and dangers of AI, developing regulatory frameworks on what AI content should be disallowed for certain audiences and making sure there is a clear chain of accountability.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits usage
sections.summary: More than half a million Singaporeans used their SkillsFuture credits last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: More than half a million Singaporeans used their SkillsFuture credits last year.

sections.label: SMEs as early adopters
sections.summary: SMEs fear being first movers after seeing technologies become outdated, so lower risk structured ways to experiment will be created.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: They tell me: "Jasmin, you want us to be early adopters, but we do not want to be the first movers." They have personal experiences of trying out new technologies and then realising that the technologies became outdated too fast.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We will create lower risk, structured ways for our SMEs to experiment.

sections.label: Shift in AI funding support
sections.summary: As AI prototypes are now quick to build, the barrier is capability and workflow redesign, so funding shifts to implementation, redesign and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: When IT adoption was the main challenge, the barrier was set-up cost, so we subsidised set-up costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Today, an early-stage AI prototype can be built in just a few hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: So, the barrier now is capability and workflow redesign.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Our funding support will shift accordingly towards implementation, business process redesign, reskilling and the much harder work of changing how an organisation actually operates.

sections.label: Education focus with AI
sections.summary: AI will force education to focus on judgement, values and working with AI rather than competing with it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: AI will force us to sharpen the focus of education on what truly matters – judgement, values and the ability to work with AI rather than compete with it.

sections.label: Children mastering AI
sections.summary: Work will be done on helping children sharpen judgement in uncertain situations so they remain master of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: How do we help them sharpen their judgement skills, especially in uncertain situations?

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: These are all areas that we will be working on, so that our children grow up confident that they remain the master of AI – and not the other way around.

sections.label: Control over AI use
sections.summary: We must intentionally decide what AI is used for, to build a smarter economy and wiser society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Most importantly, we must always be in control of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We must intentionally decide what AI should be used for, even if it nudges us to think otherwise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: This is how we can build not just a smarter economy, but a wiser and a more confident society, ready for the journey ahead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Much has been said about huge surpluses and some have asked whether we may have set aside more than was necessary and that we aimed poorly and overshot.

sections.label: Parents supporting children and parents
sections.summary: A 2019 NTUC Income survey found 94% of parents felt pressured supporting both growing children and ageing parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As far back as 2019, NTUC Income research reported that 94% of parents surveyed revealed that they were currently pressured between having to financially support their growing children and their ageing parents.

sections.label: Family schemes and Child LifeSG Credits
sections.summary: The Government provides broad-based support including $500 in Child LifeSG Credits, but many structural family schemes give extra benefits only from the third child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Government has provided broad-based support and I welcome measures, such as the additional $500 in Child LifeSG Credits in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: However, many of our structural family schemes are still designed to provide additional benefits only from the third child onwards.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax rate
sections.summary: Singapore has Asia's highest carbon tax, and the Prime Minister expects the rate to settle at the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne band by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: On carbon pricing, Singapore already has the highest carbon tax in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: So, I welcome the Prime Minister's pragmatic stance that the rate will likely settle at the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne band by 2030.

sections.label: Solar energy targets
sections.summary: Singapore met its two gigawatts peak solar target ahead of time, and revised targets of three gigawatts peak by 2030 are welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: On solar energy, we achieved our two gigawatts peak target ahead of time – an impressive feat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The revised targets to three gigawatts peak by 2030 are welcome.

sections.label: Diversifying Singapore's energy mix
sections.summary: Diversifying the energy mix through natural gas, solar, regional power imports, low-carbon solutions and potentially nuclear energy requires partnership, enabling regulations, funding mechanisms and an ecosystem of providers and off takers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Diversifying our energy mix – through natural gas, solar, regional power imports, low-carbon solutions and potentially nuclear energy – is paramount to the survival and resilience of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It requires a deeper and more deliberate partnership between Government and industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We must establish enabling regulations, dedicated funding mechanisms and a robust ecosystem of technology providers, project developers and reliable baseload off takers.

sections.label: Walkability, safety and HDB wait-out period
sections.summary: Walkability and safety should be designed for a 75-year-old with slower reflexes, and private property owners face a 15-month wait-out period before buying resale HDB flats even with legitimate right-sizing reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We should consider designing walkability and safety not for the average 30-year-old, but for the 75-year-old with slower reflexes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: There are private property owners subject to a 15-month wait-out period before purchasing resale HDB flats even when they may have legitimate reasons for needing to right-size quickly.

sections.label: AI in Budget 2026
sections.summary: In Budget 2026, AI is no longer peripheral to Singapore's plans but central to its economic strategy and future competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What stood out most to me in Budget 2026 is this: AI is no longer peripheral to Singapore's plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is central to our economic strategy and our future competitiveness.

sections.label: AI adoption for Singapore
sections.summary: AI adoption must be deep, worker-centred, inclusive, accessible to SMEs and supportive of the vulnerable, so Singapore moves fast and together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: AI adoption must be deep not cosmetic, worker-centred, inclusive by design, accessible to SMEs and supportive of the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: If we get this right, Singapore will not merely adopt AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: We will prove that a nation can move fast in this space and still move together.

sections.label: Global growth clusters
sections.summary: The Budget focuses on global growth clusters where Singapore can lead, including semiconductors, biomedical sciences, green energy, digital trust and future finance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Budget rightly zeroes in on our global growth clusters where Singapore can lead in semiconductors and advanced manufacturing; biomedical sciences; green energy and the hydrogen economy; digital trust, cybersecurity and AI; and future finance and logistics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore today produces 10% of chips globally and 20% of semiconductor equipment.

sections.label: Care subsidies and means testing
sections.summary: Budget 2026 provides higher preschool subsidies, expanded student care support and enhanced long-term care subsidies, with nuanced means testing for eldercare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 takes meaningful steps in providing for higher preschool subsidies, expanded student care support and enhanced long-term care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A more nuanced means testing approach for eldercare, one that recognises liquidity constraints, will prevent families from being priced out of essential care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Because by 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 or above.

sections.label: Simplifying access to measures
sections.summary: The next task is to make measures simple to access, aligned with employer needs and meaningful for Singaporeans, with continued focus on partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our next task is to make these measures simple to access, aligned with employer needs and meaningful for Singaporeans on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I support Budget 2026 for the clarity of the strategies to take Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I call for continued focus on simplifying access, strengthening partnerships and building community level support ecosystems.

sections.label: Tourism sector engagement
sections.summary: Engagement with tour guides and tourism sector representatives brought together business leaders, professionals, trade associations and frontline practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Eight, tour guides and representatives from the tourism sector, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This engagement brought together business leader, professionals, trade associations and frontline practitioners, enabling us to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the challenges faced by enterprise and businesses.

sections.label: Business support measures
sections.summary: The Budget proposes a corporate income tax rebate, enhancements to Enterprise Financing Schemes and higher support levels for overseas expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Budget proposes corporate income tax rebate, enhancements to Enterprise Financing Schemes and higher support levels for overseas expansion.

sections.label: Policy goal on productivity
sections.summary: The policy aims to raise productivity and not to inflate business cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The goal of our policy is to raise productivity and not to inflate business cost.

sections.label: SME cost support measures
sections.summary: It sets out transparency, tiered support to limit SME cost burdens, and subsidies for capacity building rather than just buying systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, let businesses understand clearly the cost and effect, increasing transparency; Second, tiered support to prevent SMEs from bearing excessive cost burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, subsidies are to encourage capacity building, not just to buy systems.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus and long-term spending
sections.summary: A fiscal surplus buffers the nation, but fiscal planning is not merely annual balance given ageing, healthcare, climate and technology spending needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A fiscal surplus provides a buffer for the nation, but fiscal planning has never been merely about annual balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Population ageing, rising healthcare expenditure, climate adaptation investments and technological transformation require long-term spending.

sections.label: SMEs and AI adoption costs
sections.summary: SMEs acknowledge AI is the way forward for competitiveness, but one SME was quoted a six-figure sum by an AI vendor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They acknowledged that AI is the way forward and recognise the need to embrace it in order to remain competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, one SME shared with me that when he approached an AI vendor to explore solutions for his business, he was quoted a six-figure sum, a significant investment that many smaller enterprises would understandably find daunting.

sections.label: SME partnerships with institutions
sections.summary: It asks whether, beyond grants for SMEs to engage IT vendors, stronger partnerships between SMEs and universities and polytechnics can be fostered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Beyond providing grants for SMEs to engage IT vendors, can we also foster stronger partnership between SMEs and our universities and polytechnics?

sections.label: NTUC role in linkages
sections.summary: It asks whether NTUC could be encouraged to explore a facilitated role in building such bridges or linkages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, could we also encourage NTUC to explore playing a facilitated role in building such bridge or linkages.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus size and GDP
sections.summary: The fiscal surplus is the all-time-largest in absolute terms at $15 billion, or 1.9% of GDP, versus 2.3% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The elephant in the room, which many Members have spoken about, is our fiscal surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It is the all-time-largest in absolute terms, at $15 billion for the past financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: But because our economy keeps growing, it is more appropriate to look at the fiscal surplus as a percentage of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Even by this measure, at 1.9%, it is substantial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Around 10 years ago in 2017, our surplus was at 2.3% of GDP.

sections.label: Corporate income tax after COVID-19
sections.summary: Corporate income tax collections have been far higher after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Zooming out, the multi-year picture is that corporate income tax collections have been far higher after COVID-19.

sections.label: Citizen population without immigration
sections.summary: Without immigration, the number of Singaporeans will more than halve each generation and could revert by SG100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: At current levels of fertility and without immigration, the number of Singaporeans will more than halve in each generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: By SG100, without immigration, our citizen population could even revert to the same size as when we first became independent.

sections.label: Elderly poverty and Silver Support
sections.summary: Elderly poverty should be eradicated, with increased Silver Support and the highest tier for seniors above 80 or 85 in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Elderly poverty should be eradicated, especially for the generations that grew up in a less developed Singapore and without the lifelong support of retirement policies that are in place today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I continue to advocate for Silver Support payouts to be increased and for the highest tier of Silver Support to be given to seniors above the age of 80 or 85 who live in HDB flats.

sections.label: Returning surpluses as CDC vouchers
sections.summary: Fiscal surpluses above 2% of GDP should be given back to all Singaporeans the following year through extra CDC vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: For example, any fiscal surpluses above 2% of GDP should be given back to all Singaporeans in the following year through extra CDC vouchers.

sections.label: Free basic childcare and student care
sections.summary: Basic childcare, infant care and student care should be free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: First, basic childcare, infant care and student care should be free.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus and revenue moves
sections.summary: The fiscal surplus should give the Government confidence to assure Singaporeans it would not take major revenue raising moves up to 2035, barring material adverse circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Fourth and finally, amidst continued cost of living anxieties, the fiscal surplus should give the Government more confidence to assure Singaporeans that it would not take major revenue raising moves up to 2035, barring any material adverse circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Thus far, it has only said that it would not raise GST until 2030.

sections.label: Tax policies and wealth inequality
sections.summary: Tax policies should be used to reduce wealth inequality through a more progressive property tax system, higher taxes for investment properties and progressive stamp duties on inherited properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We should continue to use tax policies to achieve other objectives, such as reducing wealth inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: This can be achieved by making our property tax system more progressive, by being more aggressive with taxes for investment properties and by imposing progressive stamp duties on properties at the point of inheritance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Ensuring that we do not tax more than we need to spend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And if there are surprises in our fiscal projections, it is better to be surprised by a surplus and never by a deficit.

sections.label: Conservative fiscal projections and surplus sharing
sections.summary: The speaker says fiscal projections should stay conservative and unexpected budget surpluses should be shared systematically with all Singaporeans the next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: My takeaway from his speech was that Mr Giam was suggesting that we run less conservative fiscal projections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: My suggestion and my view is that we should still be conservative with our fiscal projections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: And twined with my idea that if we run unexpected budget surpluses, we should have that as a systematic surplus sharing mechanism in the next year with all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Actually, I think we are on the same page.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I do believe that we should run a small surplus whenever possible, but that is different from running a surplus that is $8.29 billion more than what was estimated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And I think he himself suggested that surpluses over 2% should be given back the following year.

sections.label: Last financial year budget surplus
sections.summary: In the last financial year, a budget surplus of more than 2% was not run.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: In fact, in the last financial year we did not run a budget surplus of more than 2%.

sections.label: PMET share of employed residents
sections.summary: According to MOM's report on the Labour Force in Singapore 2025, 64% of employed residents are in PMET roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: According to MOM's report on the Labour Force in Singapore 2025, 64% of our employed residents are in PMET roles.

sections.label: Workforce exposure to AI
sections.summary: Singapore's workforce is highly exposed to AI due to the large share of such roles in the economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Singapore’s workforce is highly exposed to AI due to the large share of such roles in our economy.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator expansion to professions
sections.summary: Expanding the TechSkills Accelerator to accountancy and legal professions strengthens capability-building in sectors facing talent and retention challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In particular, the expansion of the TechSkills Accelerator to the accountancy and legal professions presents opportunities by strengthening capability-building in these sectors, which are facing ongoing talent and retention challenges.

sections.label: AI adoption and foreign companies
sections.summary: Supporting in-house legal counsels and accountants in AI adoption strengthens Singapore's attractiveness to foreign companies, as these groups may be missed by firm-targeted initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Supporting them in their adoption of AI will also strengthen Singapore's attractiveness to foreign companies looking to hire Singaporeans or to set up headquarters in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: These in-house legal counsels and accountants may not be fully reached by initiatives targeted at law firms and accounting practices.

sections.label: Champions of AI for small SMEs
sections.summary: The Champions of AI programme tailors support to each company, and the speaker hopes it will be considered alongside the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and Productivity Solutions Grant for micro- and small SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The newly announced Champions of AI programme will go some way to support this by tailoring support to each company, including enterprise transformation and workforce training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider the Champions of AI programme alongside the more established schemes, such as the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and the Productivity Solutions Grant to marry the two for micro- and small SMEs, who often face their own unique sets of constraints on cashflows, cost, implementation expertise and change management.

sections.label: Uneven take-up of family workplace support
sections.summary: Take-up of family related workplace support remains uneven, and MOM and NTUC work with partners on flexible work norms and return-to-work pathways through tripartite guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Despite stronger policies, take-up of family related workplace support across employers and employees remain uneven, reflecting the continued influence of workplace expectations and culture on employees' confidence to take time for family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: MOM and NTUC have been working with their partners on this front to set clearer norms for flexible work arrangements, to help enterprises understand how to structure return-to-work pathways and job design that accommodates caregiving responsibilities, through tripartite guidelines and programmes with industry partners.

sections.label: HR practices for family-friendly workplaces
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government works with industry partners like the tripartite Institute for Human Resource Professionals to shape HR practices emphasising fair family-friendly implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The difference lies in how workplaces interpret and respond to these moments, and how managers are equipped to communicate with care, make balanced decisions and plan for continuity without placing undue strain on teams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can work with the industry partners, such as the tripartite Institute for Human Resource Professionals, to shape HR practices and standards across industries to place greater emphasis on consistent and fair implementation of family-friendly workplace practices.

sections.label: Aligned system for opportunity and resilience
sections.summary: A system aligned across education, workplaces and support structures lets individuals decide with confidence and contribute over time, strengthening opportunity and resilience in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: A system that is aligned across education, workplaces and support structures, gives individuals the space to make decisions with confidence and to contribute meaningfully over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This is how we can strengthen both opportunity and resilience in Singapore.

sections.label: AI job displacement and creation
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates AI could displace 92 million jobs and create 170 million new roles by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum estimates that by 2030, AI and related technologies could displace 92 million jobs, while creating 170 million new roles, reflecting a profound structural shift in how work is done.

sections.label: Singapore AI skills gap
sections.summary: AWS-commissioned research found 94% of Singapore employers expect AI-driven employees by 2028, but 74% struggle to find AI talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Research commissioned by Amazon Web Services (AWS) on AI adoption and skills in Singapore found that nearly 94% of employers expect their employees to be AI-driven by 2028, yet, 74% report difficulty finding the AI talent they need, highlighting a clear skills gap between demand and supply.

sections.label: Gen Z AI skills interest
sections.summary: The same AWS research showed 91% of Singapore Generation Z want to acquire AI skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The same AWS research also showed that 91% of Generation Z in Singapore want to acquire AI skills, underscoring both the urgency and willingness of our youths to embrace this transformation.

sections.label: Personal Learning Devices for students
sections.summary: Singapore has provided Personal Learning Devices to all secondary students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore has already taken a decisive step by providing Personal Learning Devices (PLDs) to all secondary students.

sections.label: Primary school PLD progress update
sections.summary: The speaker says such access lays groundwork for AI literacy and requests an update on primary school PLD progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Such access would lay the groundwork for future AI literacy, ensuring that all students – all students – regardless of background, can engage fully with digital and AI-enabled learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am unsure of the progress MOE has made in introducing PLDs at the primary school level since my last advocacy and would, therefore, like to request for an update on any developments on how we can best equip our younger learners for the demands of a digital and AI-driven future.

sections.label: EdTech Masterplan and Budget 2026
sections.summary: The EdTech Masterplan 2030 makes digital literacy a national priority, aligning with Budget 2026's AI strategic advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As Singapore's EdTech Masterplan 2030 reflects, strengthening students' digital literacy and technological skills is a national priority to, "prepare students for a technology transformed world".

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, access to appropriate hardware ensures that all students – all students – regardless of background, can engage effectively with emerging digital tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This aligns with Budget 2026, which highlights harnessing AI as a strategic advantage to build a resilient and skilled workforce.

sections.label: Equitable access to PLDs
sections.summary: The passage calls equitable access to PLDs in primary schools a strategic investment and renews a call to extend PLDs to primary students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this way, equitable access to PLDs in primary schools is not merely an educational measure, but a strategic investment in Singapore's long-term human capital and technological competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to renew my call to the Government to make that decision to extend PLDs to primary school students.

sections.label: Graduate Industry Traineeships Programme expansion
sections.summary: The passage states the Graduate Industry Traineeships Programme was introduced last year and says traineeships should be expanded to more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government introduced the Graduate Industry Traineeships Programme last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition to financial services and information and communications, traineeships should be expanded to include the newly announced focus sectors in Singapore's AI strategy – advanced manufacturing, connectivity and even healthcare – as well as people-centric industries, such as social services sectors and retail.

sections.label: S Pass salary benchmarks
sections.summary: The passage says higher S Pass minimum qualifying salaries may require a sector-based, skills-focused approach for construction and that benchmarks should reflect skills, experience and responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the increase in minimum qualifying salaries for S Pass holders, a more sector-based and skills-focused approach may be needed for construction, where structural manpower shortages persist and margins are unhealthily eroded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Salary benchmarks should better reflect skills, experience and job responsibilities, rather than relying heavily on age tiers alone.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and flexi-work
sections.summary: The passage proposes doubling down on SkillsFuture for parents and making flexi-work arrangements a mainstream feature of good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One starting point is to double down on SkillsFuture for these parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Flexi-work arrangements should become a mainstream feature of good jobs – not an exception, but an integral part of how we attract, retain and empower workers across every life stage.

sections.label: Seniors employment in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that to assist seniors in employment, Singapore is set to become a super-aged society this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Fourth, to assist our seniors in employment, Singapore is set to become a super-aged society this year.

sections.label: Mature workers matching service
sections.summary: The passage describes the AfA-EMW pilot programme and suggests a matching service connecting industry veterans with SMEs as consultants, experts or trainers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, the Alliance for Action on Empowering Multi-Stage Careers for Mature Workers (AfA-EMW) launched a pilot programme, collaborating with various parties to jointly create solutions for re-skilling, alternative employment models and progressive retirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While this is a positive start, we should also care for those seniors who prefer a low commitment but high impact work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest establishing a matching service, such as connecting industry veterans with SMEs to serve as consultants, subject matter experts or trainers.

sections.label: Quality ageing and senior dignity
sections.summary: Quality ageing involves not only financial security but also providing seniors a space to live with dignity and purpose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Quality ageing is not only about financial security but also about providing our seniors with a space where they can live with dignity and purpose for years to come.

sections.label: Silver Support and household income

sentences.text: The scheme is well-intentioned and has benefited many seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, I have received appeals from residents whose Silver Support payments were reduced or ceased due to changes in per capita household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, when adult children begin working, even in modest-paying jobs, their parents' Silver Support may be reduced despite no improvement in the seniors' own retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Seniors worry about becoming a burden, while younger families struggle to balance caregiving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)

sections.label: Wage support percentages

sentences.text: Today, wage support can reach up to 70%, and up to 90% for eligible workers aged 40 and above.

sections.label: Preventive Health Data Sandbox proposal

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In tandem, a national certification framework for preventive AI algorithms could strengthen international credibility, enabling solutions validated here to be deployed across the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is already taking important steps through research, innovation and enterprise investments and initiatives such as subsidised Familial Hypercholesterolaemia genetic screening with MediSave support.

sections.label: Blended capital for health
