sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is well-positioned to mobilise blended capital, as foundations, philanthropies and family offices increasingly prioritise investments in wellness, longevity and population health.

sections.label: Biomedical science and AI platforms
sections.summary: Combining biomedical science, AI and diagnostics strengths lets local enterprises create globally deployable preventive health platforms, analytics tools and healthspan solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By combining our strengths in biomedical science, AI and diagnostics, local enterprises can create globally deployable preventive health platforms, personalised analytics tools and healthspan solutions.

sections.label: Budget surplus size
sections.summary: A Budget surplus of $15.1 billion is likely the largest in absolute terms since 1965.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, a Budget surplus of $15.1 billion is likely the largest in absolute terms since 1965.

sections.label: Surplus use and reserves
sections.summary: The speaker supports setting aside about half the surplus as strategic reserves and using the remaining half for targeted welfare, especially vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Given the global geopolitical tensions and economic volatility, I support setting aside about half of the surplus as strategic reserves, in the event that there might be economic crisis in the next few three or four years, so that it can be used to stimulate the economy and support Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: But the remaining half should be used in a targeted manner to enhance our people's welfare, particularly the vulnerable groups.

sections.label: GST increase revenue
sections.summary: The two-percentage points GST increase will yield an estimated $3 billion to $4 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The two-percentage points GST increase will yield an estimated $3 billion to $4 billion annually.

sections.label: Extra CDC vouchers proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government distribute an extra $200 CDC vouchers to Singaporeans over 21 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Hence, the same amount does not mean equality here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I will like to suggest that the Government distribute an extra $200 CDC vouchers to Singaporeans over 21 years old.

sections.label: Support for special needs adults
sections.summary: Support for adults with special needs remains limited, with insufficient opportunities for vocational training, retraining, or workforce reintegration after setbacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Currently, support for adults with special needs remains limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Opportunities for continuous vocational training, skills retraining, or reintegrating into the workforce after experiencing setbacks are still insufficient.

sections.label: Special needs foundation proposal
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to consider allocating dedicated resources to establish a special needs foundation for long-term projects, research and community support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For these families, the issue is no longer about opportunities, but about dignity, stability and peace of mind for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hereby call upon the Government to consider allocating dedicated resources to establish a special needs foundation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This foundation could fund long-term projects, research and community support to, where possible, help adults with special needs, maintain employability and stay connected with society and provide empathetic and structured care for those with special needs who cannot work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Let us walk along persons with special needs, not only during their childhood but throughout their entire lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It represents the collective sacrifices made by workers, businesses and families during difficult times through paying taxes, adapting to GST increases and tightening their belts.

sections.label: NTUC survey on economic sentiments
sections.summary: NTUC's 2025 survey of 2,000 workers found cost of living, job security and AI concerns among workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As the Secretary-General of the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), I am keenly aware that for many of our workers and families, these disruptive forces are not distant issues but daily lived experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This is reflected in NTUC's Survey on Economic Sentiments, which was conducted in 2025 polling 2,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Cost of living remains a key concern – 37%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Job security was the top concern for nearly 20% of them too, due to factors, such as economic uncertainties and technological changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Close to 20% were anxious about artificial intelligence (AI)-related job displacement or had already experienced some negative impact due to AI.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG funding support
sections.summary: Through AI-Ready SG, union members get NTUC funding to offset up to 50% of unfunded subscription costs for eligible AI tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Concretely, through AI-Ready SG, union members will get NTUC funding support to offset up to 50% of unfunded subscription costs for eligible AI tools.

sections.label: Employer and PME job anxiety
sections.summary: An SNEF survey found 60% of employers planned headcount freezes, and NTUC found almost 40% of PMEs anxious about jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Among the employers polled in a survey by the Singapore National Employers' Federation (SNEF), nearly three in five, or 60%, planned to freeze headcount this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC's own survey found that almost 40% of PMEs were anxious about whether they could still keep their jobs beyond the next six months.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support income cap
sections.summary: Only workers earning $5,000 or less monthly qualify for JSS, and exceeding this cap caused 60% of rejections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Today, only workers earning $5,000 or less monthly are eligible for the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As of September 2025, exceeding this income cap was one of the reasons for 60% of applications to be rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: One possible approach is to peg the income threshold to the professional, manager, executive and technician (PMET) median monthly income, which was around $7,600 in 2025.

sections.label: NTUC support for workers and PMEs
sections.summary: NTUC will work with Government and employers to help workers be AI-ready and support PMEs, and the speaker supports the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: NTUC will continue to work with the Government and employers to ensure that every worker can stand on firm footing during the transitions, with peace of mind at work and at home. : Mr Speaker, the challenges of this disrupted age require us to do more to strengthen ourselves from within.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Let us empower every worker be AI-ready, strengthen support to those vulnerable to disruption and strengthen the Labour Movement's ability to protect and uplift our PMEs in this age where it is no longer just the blue-collar workers that may face technological disruption, but with AI disrupting the white-collar space as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement will continue advocating for measures that support workers today and improve their prospects for tomorrow, whether it is helping young graduates into good first jobs, supporting PMEs to navigate career transitions or ensuring caregivers can stay employed while caring for their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the points I have raised on behalf of the Labour Movement, I stand in support of this Budget.

sections.label: Global and demographic trends
sections.summary: The passage cites projected skills changes by 2030, rising tariffs, a super-aged society and a low fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report projects that nearly 40% of skills being used in today's workforce will change by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Global trade tensions continue to intensify, with the value of goods hit by new tariffs quadrupling in the past year to the highest level in over 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of this year, we are now an officially super-aged society, with more than 21% of our resident population 65 or above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, our resident total fertility rate (TFR) stands at less than half the replacement rate.

sections.label: Citizens aged 80 and older
sections.summary: The number of citizens aged 80 and older increased by about 60% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of citizens aged 80 and older have increased by approximately 60% over the past decade.

sections.label: Older workforce and Malay TFR
sections.summary: The passage calls for considering social and emotional dimensions of an older workforce, and states Malay TFR is 1.58 in 2024, below replacement rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Having said the above, we should also consider the social and emotional dimensions of how an older workforce responds to such rapid change and support them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, the reality we must face is that the TFR of Malays is now below the population replacement rate, at 1.58 in 2024.

sections.label: Seniors needing daily living assistance
sections.summary: The passage says more support is needed and that by 2030 around 100,000 seniors are expected to require assistance with daily living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, in an era of rapid change, more support is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that every family in Singapore will continue to have faith – that we will stand together through thick and thin and remain confident that the prosperity we build will be inclusive and benefit every family. : By 2030, around 100,000 seniors are expected to require assistance with daily living.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant and caregivers
sections.summary: The passage welcomes HCG enhancements, describes caregiving pressures on women, and hopes qualifying criteria include those unable to work due to mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Enhancements to the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) are very welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, many rely on annual leave and career often competes with caregiving responsibilities until a point where one feels like they have to tap out of the workforce, especially for women who tend to disproportionately carry the caregiving load; having stronger caregiver support frameworks, including hospital post-discharge protocols, as well as helping caregivers begin again after their loved ones are no longer around.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope we broaden the qualifying criteria of the HCG to include those who are unable to work due to mental health conditions, instead of only assessing by activities of daily living.

sections.label: Singaporeans over 65 by 2050
sections.summary: By 2050, nearly half of Singaporeans are projected to be over 65.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: By 2050, nearly half of Singaporeans are projected to be over 65.

sections.label: Projected surplus of $15 billion
sections.summary: The projected surplus of $15 billion is more than double the earlier estimate of $7 billion and is a stark reminder of a recurring pattern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The projected surplus of $15 billion, more than double the earlier estimate of $7 billion, is a stark reminder of a recurring pattern.

sections.label: GST hike revenue projections
sections.summary: GST hike was projected to bring $3.5 billion annually by 2024, with revenue rising from $12.8 billion in 2022 to $22.3 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It begs the question of whether the urgency behind tax increases, such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) hike, was truly justified when the state consistently finds itself with more resources than initially projected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And also, based on my checks, when announced in 2022, the GST hike was projected to bring about $3.5 billion annually when the full hike is in place by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: GST revenue was initially estimated at $12.8 billion in Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This year, GST revenue is estimated at $22.3 billion, an almost $10 billion increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The most notable of which is the exclusion of land sale proceeds, amounting to $21 billion in 2025 and estimated at $21 billion in 2026.

sections.label: Corporate income tax rebate
sections.summary: The corporate income tax rebate for Budget 2026 was reduced to 40%, compared to 50% for 2024 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To underscore my point, the corporate income tax rebate for Budget 2026 was reduced to 40%, compared to 50% for 2024 and 2025.

sections.label: MOF wealth inequality paper
sections.summary: MOF's Occasional Paper published 9 February provided the first-ever public release of Singapore's wealth data, showing a Gini coefficient of 0.55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I was initially hopeful, when the recently released the Ministry of Finance's (MOF's) Occasional Paper on "Income Growth, Inequality and Social Mobility Trends in Singapore" was published on 9 February, ahead of Prime Minister Wong's Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This paper provided the first-ever public release of Singapore's wealth data, which revealed that Singapore's wealth inequality, with a Gini coefficient of 0.55, exceeds that of income inequality.

sections.label: Net Annual Value tax proposal
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates a Budget 2023 proposal to reinstate a Net Annual Value tax on properties, targeting high-end properties and secondary residences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This data underscores the urgency of implementing robust measures to address wealth disparities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I reiterate my proposal from my Budget 2023 for a Net Annual Value (NAV) tax on properties to be reinstated, particularly targeting high-end properties such as Good Class Bungalows or those who own secondary residences.

sections.label: Estate duty reinstatement
sections.summary: The speaker says estate duty, abolished in 2008, must be seriously considered for reinstatement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we must seriously consider bringing back estate duty, which was abolished in 2008.

sections.label: PARF rebate for BMW
sections.summary: A BMW 5-series listed around $370,000 will see its PARF rebate cut from around $40,000 to $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A BMW 5-series, listed for around $370,000 will see its PARF rebate slashed from around $40,000 to $4,000.

sections.label: Falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR fell below 1.0 in 2023 and stayed there in 2024, threatening long-term sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our TFR fell below 1.0 in 2023 and remained there in 2024, a trajectory that poses a profound threat to our long-term sustainability.

sections.label: Hungary mothers income tax exemption
sections.summary: Hungary exempts mothers of three children from personal income tax, and from this year mothers under 30 with one child too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The point here is this, that Hungary is fully exempting mothers with three children from paying personal income tax regardless of age and starting this year, even mothers under 30 with at least one child will be fully exempt.

sections.label: Childcare subsidies and LifeSG Credits
sections.summary: This year's Budget raised the childcare subsidy income ceiling from $12,000 to $15,000 and gives $500 LifeSG Credits to families with children under 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As part of this year's Budget package, the household income ceiling for childcare subsidies was increased from $12,000 to $15,000, while families with children below 12 years old will receive $500 in LifeSG Credits.

sections.label: Projected 2025 surplus
sections.summary: The projected surplus for 2025 is $15.1 billion, more than double the initial estimate of $6.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The projected surplus for 2025 stands at $15.1 billion, more than double the initial estimate of $6.8 billion.

sections.label: GST revenue and wealth taxes
sections.summary: GST revenue rose from $12.8 billion to a projected $22.3 billion, and the passage calls for wealth tax measures to address inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The estimated total GST revenue then was $12.8 billion, whilst this year, this figure is projected to soar to $22.3 billion, an increase of nearly $10 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, addressing wealth inequality has become urgent, as emphasised by the MOF’s recent Occasional Paper on this challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We need to adopt bold measures, such as re-introducing NAV tax, reconsidering estate tax and exploring innovative wealth tax models like those in Switzerland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Drawing from international experience, we must formulate comprehensive and structural solutions that give Singaporeans the confidence and capability to start families.

sections.label: Equitable resilient social contract
sections.summary: The passage asks whether to collect less tax from the surplus or let demographics wither while wealth concentrates, urging a more equitable social contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Is it collecting a few percentage points less in taxes from our record-breaking surplus or allowing the nation's demographic foundation to wither whilst wealth concentrates in the hands of a select few, leaving middle-class Singaporeans to foot the bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Let us build a more equitable, resilient and sustainable social contract.

sections.label: Five groups of workers
sections.summary: The Budget will address five groups of workers called the "5 U's": unemployed, underemployed, under-represented, untrained and under-served.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: If we ask workers to work hard, upgrade, adapt, we must also ask the economy to deliver real outcomes for them. “When workers do everything right but still feel left behind, the problem is not their effort, it is the system.” This is why, in this Budget, I will speak for five groups of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I call them the "5 U's" – the unemployed, the underemployed, the under-represented, the untrained and the under-served.

sections.label: Advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications
sections.summary: Introducing advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications to unions and the Government can provide more timely and early intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, introducing advanced Mandatory Retrenchment Notifications (MRNs) to unions and the Government can provide more timely and early intervention.

sections.label: Sharing disruption information, raising income threshold
sections.summary: The Government can consider sharing disruption information with NTUC and unions, and raising the JSS income threshold from $5,000 to $7,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, the Government can consider sharing information with NTUC and unions on sectors and companies that might be disrupted due to economic restructuring, including expected scale of impact and timeline, past retrenchment incidence, and past retrenchment benefit levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am heartened that after a decade of lobbying, involuntarily unemployed workers facing temporary financial strain can now benefit from transitional support for up to six months while they undergo training or look for better-fitting jobs through the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme (JSS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, from April to August last year, MOM also shared that 60% of the 7,200 JSS applications received were rejected, of which one of the top three reasons for unsuccessful applications was exceeding the income threshold of $5,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Government can consider raising the income threshold from $5,000 to $7,600 to better cover PMEs.

sections.label: Graduate employment survey findings
sections.summary: Recent Graduate Employment Surveys show fewer graduates secured permanent full-time positions within six months across universities, private institutions and polytechnics, even as starting salaries rose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: According to the most recent Graduate Employment Surveys from autonomous universities, private education institutions and polytechnics, fewer graduates secured permanent full-time positions within six months of graduation across the board, even as starting salaries continued to rise.

sections.label: GRIT Programme for graduates
sections.summary: The Government launched the GRIT Programme last year to absorb employers' recruitment and training risk while helping fresh graduates gain industry experience and skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Government launched the GRIT Programme last year to absorb recruitment and training risk for employers while helping fresh graduates gain industry experience and relevant skills.

sections.label: EDB jobs created at 20-year low
sections.summary: The Economic Development Board announced a 20-year-low number of jobs expected to be created, despite attracting more investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Economic Development Board (EDB) recently announced a 20-year-low number of jobs expected to be created, despite attracting more investments.

sections.label: Employment Act Part IV thresholds
sections.summary: A call to raise Employment Act Part IV income thresholds for non-workmen to at least $3,000 and review the Act regularly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Lower-income PMEs, sometimes disguised, for example, are not covered under Part IV of the Employment Act which provides for rest days, hours of work and overtime pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to increase the Employment Act Part IV income thresholds, something that I raised in this House before, for non-workmen to at least $3,000, which will better reflect today's workforce demographics and help curb overworking norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To ensure protections in the Employment Act keep pace with wage growth and workforce changes, the Government can commit to reviewing the Employment Act every five years or when salaries reach a particular threshold, with a mid-term review of income thresholds to ensure legislation does not lag economic shifts.

sections.label: Foreign PME qualifying salaries
sections.summary: Welcomes raising qualifying salaries for EP and S Pass holders to keep their quality as wages rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The key is to create policy that encourages foreign PMEs to complement rather than displace the local workforce, encourage skill transfer and local-foreign integration and position local PMEs for senior and leadership positions as well as high-paying and high-value jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Government's decision to raise the qualifying salaries for and S Pass holders to maintain the quality of EP and S Pass holders as wages rise.

sections.label: Merging WSG and SSG
sections.summary: Welcomes a new one-stop agency merging WSG and SSG for skills training, career guidance and job matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: During SkillsFuture's 10th anniversary last year, I suggested to consolidate efforts and streamline offerings across different arms of the CET ecosystem including NTUC's e2i, WSG, SSG, training providers and the various Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), to control quality and prevent overlap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government considered the recommendation and are going to create now a one-stop-shop new agency for skills training, career guidance and job matching services by merging WSG and SSG.

sections.label: NTUC AI training subsidies
sections.summary: NTUC will roll out AI training pathways and subsidise up to 50% of eligible AI tool subscription costs for members for two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: NTUC will roll out AI training pathways and subsidise up to 50% of subscription costs of eligible AI tools for members, for an initial period of two years.

sections.label: UEC and EEC employment credits
sections.summary: Calls for considering an extension of the UEC, which ended December 2025, and continued inclusive hiring support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Uplifting Employment Credit (UEC) for ex-offenders and the Enabling Employment Credit (EEC) for persons with disabilities, which provide employers with wage offsets to enhance employment support for disconnected individuals and widen our labour pool, are commendable initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government continues to embed inclusive hiring into mainstream workforce policy to unlock under-utilised potential and ensure all workers can contribute fully and justly, as well as to boost the employment and employability of ex-offenders and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I note that the UEC scheme ended on December 2025, and I ask that an extension be considered.

sections.label: Tripartite workgroup on Employment Act
sections.summary: States there are tripartite negotiations and a Tripartite Workgroup reviewing the Employment Act, while NTUC's standpoint was shared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Shortly thereafter, the chief executive officer (CEO) of SNEF wrote to The Straits Times to share that, I think the words were: "they have strong reservations about this call." Can I ask the Member, in view of the tripartite framework, has there been agreement with SNEF on this particular point?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: On the Member's question, there are tripartite negotiations on this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: We have formed a Tripartite Workgroup on the review of the Employment Act which I am a member, we are looking at this carefully to balance the interests of the respective tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: But what I shared earlier is our NTUC's standpoint, which both Secretary-General and myself have shared earlier.

sections.label: HDB blocks and Budget surplus
sections.summary: More HDB blocks are crossing 50 years, and the 2025 Budget surplus of over $15 billion will be added to reserves for investment income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But more and more of our HDB blocks are also crossing the 50-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is good news indeed that we had managed to achieve a Budget surplus of over $15 billion for 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The surplus will be added to our reserves, where we can generate investment income streams that will contribute to our future Budgets.

sections.label: Review of HDB HIP policy
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether HDB can review its HIP policy and consider an additional, more flexible round of HIP for deteriorating blocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As the HDB Home Improvement Programme (HIP) takes place only twice during the span of the 99 years, residents are left waiting and are appealing for a more lasting and sustained solution to the myriad of problems affecting their blocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To deal with the systemic deterioration of such HDB blocks, could the HDB review its HIP policy and consider an additional round of HIP which is more flexible in scope to take into account the specific issues faced by a particular HDB estate?

sections.label: EASE programme for private estates
sections.summary: The Government has confirmed that the EASE programme will be offered to seniors living in private estates from this April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, the Government has confirmed that the EASE programme will be offered to seniors living in private estates from this April.

sections.label: Longer-term property tax rebate
sections.summary: A speaker hopes the Government can consider granting a longer-term rebate for seniors facing higher property taxes paid from savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The anxiety is real, especially as they are no longer earning an income and yet face increasingly higher property taxes that they are paying for out of their own savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider granting a longer-term rebate for such cases.

sections.label: Take-up rate of initiatives
sections.summary: A speaker is concerned that take-up rates for such initiatives will not be as high as desired, citing SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My concern, however, is that the take-up rate for such initiatives will not be as high as desired, given what we have seen with the SkillsFuture credits where many people left it to the final months, and even then, it was not fully taken up.

sections.label: Expanding SG Digital Community Hubs
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether IMDA's SG Digital Community Hubs can be expanded to help seniors and Singaporeans gain AI skills and safety tips.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA’s) SG Digital Community Hubs be expanded to help seniors and more Singaporeans gain AI skills and pick up safety tips?

sections.label: AI resources and support
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to make AI resources more accessible, expand SG Digital Community Hubs for seniors, and provide stronger career guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned about the potential low take-up as with SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to make AI resources more easily accessible, expand SG Digital Community Hubs to help seniors and providing stronger career guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: More resources to extend AI Missions to additional sectors and to redesign workflows and job scopes will raise productivity and ease labour shortages. : Sir, for all our hard work to achieve success, as individuals, as a nation, we need the support and assurance of safe and comfortable homes and estates for our families and secure the future of our economy and jobs in the AI age.

sections.label: Medium-term fiscal projections
sections.summary: MOF's 2023 Occasional Paper projects total spending rising to around 19.5% of GDP by 2030, driven by healthcare for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: MOF's Occasional Paper on Medium-Term Fiscal Projections in 2023 sends a very clear signal – our total spending will go up to around 19.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030, driven by healthcare for an ageing population.

sections.label: Budget 2026 revenue milestone
sections.summary: Budget 2026 is the first Budget since the Occasional Paper to reach 19.5% of GDP in total revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 is a milestone in the sense that it is the first Budget since the Occasional Paper to hit that 19.5% of GDP in total revenues.

sections.label: GST collection increase
sections.summary: With the headline GST rate rising from 7% to 9%, GST collection rose from around 2% of GDP to 2.6% in Budget 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: With the increase in headline GST rate from 7% to 9%, GST collection has gone up from around 2% of GDP to 2.6% in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Property and stamp duty rates
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising property tax collections to 1.2% of GDP and making stamp duty more progressive, with a 15% tier above $5 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But not too long ago, in the early 2000s, property tax collections were as high as 1% to 1.1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I think we should aim to raise property tax collections to 1.2% of GDP in the long term and focus on the top tier of residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Stamp duty collections stand at 0.8% of GDP in Budget 2026 and have largely been so for the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I think we should make stamp duty much more progressive in the long term with, for example, a new tier for residential properties above $5 million, at marginal rate of 15%, 2.5 times the current top marginal rate.

sections.label: Past surpluses and deficit
sections.summary: In FYs 2016 to 2019 there were Budget surpluses of 1.4%, 2.3% and 0.7% of GDP, and a deficit of $51.6 billion, 10.8% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: In FYs 2016 to 2019, we had a pretty good run – Budget surpluses of 1.4%, 2.3% and 0.7% of GDP, successively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: A deficit of $51.6 billion, 10.8% of GDP, to fight the crisis of a generation.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus comparisons
sections.summary: The speaker says FY2025's 1.9% of GDP surplus and FY2026's 1% surplus are modest, citing FY2000's 2.4% surplus and 0.6% cumulative surplus over the last term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And further back, in FY2000, we had a surplus of 2.4% of GDP, although it was just $4 billion in dollar terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And so, in my view, the surplus for FY2025 at 1.9% of GDP is somewhat modest, hardly the greatest fiscal surplus any PAP Government has seen in decades; and the surplus for FY2026 at 1% of GDP is decidedly modest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The accumulated surplus over the last term of Government, including the surplus for FY2025, is at around 0.6% of cumulative GDP, again, decidedly modest in my view.

sections.label: Extending GST offsets
sections.summary: Part of the surpluses would be ploughed back to extend transitional GST offsets by one more year for the vast majority of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Plough back part of the surpluses to extend our transitional GST offsets by one more year for the vast majority of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Balance of spending and saving
sections.summary: The speaker says balance concerns societal spending and saving, and combined two versions of a line after Minister of State Jasmin Lau's exhortation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: My idea of balance that I prompted you on was not so much about keeping versus sharing at the individual level, but about spending and saving at the societal level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Take only what is needed, leave the rest as sustenance for God's nature".

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But I really liked the second line from the first version, so responding to the Minister of State Jasmin Lau's exhortation yesterday, I exercised my human agency and critical thinking, and I combined the two versions.

sections.label: FY2021 and FY2023 balances
sections.summary: The speaker says FY2021 had a surplus of 0.3% of GDP and FY2023 a deficit of 0.4% of GDP, which were largely balanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: The surplus that we had for FY2021 was just 0.3% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In FY2023, we had a deficit of 0.4% of GDP – and I took those to be largely balanced.

sections.label: GST and spending needs
sections.summary: The speaker cites the 2023 MOF Occasional Paper saying spending needs reach 19% to 20% of GDP by 2030, and GST yields 0.6% of GDP more, from 2% to 2.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: For the first, I would say, let us go back to the MOF Occasional Paper published in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And it is stated very clearly in that paper that our total spending needs will hit 19% to 20% of GDP by 2030; the midpoint is 19.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: If the Member had listened to my speech and looked at the data, GST even with the increase from 7% to 9% headline rate, is yielding 0.6% of GDP more revenues – from 2% to 2.6% in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: GST alone hardly covers us up to the 19.5% target.

sections.label: Population planning parameter question
sections.summary: The speaker says the ruling party uses 6.9 million as a population planning parameter and should explain the limit in the population plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the ruling party uses 6.9 million as a population planning parameter, they should at least give Singaporeans an explanation – what exactly is the limit in the population plan?

sections.label: 6.9 million planning parameter
sections.summary: The Government said 6.9 million remains a planning parameter for the 2030s, with population size depending on demographic trends and social and economic needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government last month said in response to Aljunied MP Fadli Fawzi's question that, while the oft quoted number of 6.9 million is still a relevant planning parameter for the 2030s, our population size, not limits, depend on demographic trends and social and economic needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If 6.9 million is just a planning parameter, then the question Singaporeans living in high density communities like Sengkang need to see answered is this: at that parameter, what precisely does our infrastructure plan to provide and at what point does this provision start to cause discomfort?

sections.label: Regional population projections request
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government would release population projections for each region as part of Urban Redevelopment Authority plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To relieve concerns, would the Government consider releasing population projections for each region as part of the Urban Redevelopment Authority's plans?

sections.label: Dependency ratio and care work
sections.summary: It states that population and demographics are intertwined with the rising dependency ratio, a megatrend, and its implications for care work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Next, population and demographics are intertwined with our rising dependency ratio, megatrend and its implications for care work.

sections.label: Beijing lottery and births
sections.summary: A 2018 Journal of Development Economics study found Beijing's vehicle licence plate lottery was associated with fewer births among participants' households and citywide.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, research published in the Journal of Development Economics in 2018 found that the Beijing vehicle licence plate lottery system was associated with a 35% reduction in births in households of lottery participants and a 6% reduction in births across the entire city.

sections.label: Domestic worker rest day rule
sections.summary: It asks whether the 2021 rule requiring employers to give domestic workers one non-compensable rest day a month has been reassessed, and about HSS childminding services.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2021, a rule was introduced, requiring employers to provide domestic workers at least one rest day a month that cannot be compensated away.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Has the Government more recently assessed if it is enough?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With basic childminding services no longer being supported with manpower concessions under the HSS pilot from next month, is the Government working with providers to raise awareness of more general HSS services under the scheme?

sections.label: In-person play and IQ concerns
sections.summary: It cites concerns about in-person play, the Flynn effect plateauing, and other countries' laws, proposing a Select Committee to study a ban.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is concerning as in-person play develops critical social and coping skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There has also been increasing concern about the plateauing of or even reversal of the Flynn effect, which states that younger generations score higher on IQ test compared with the previous ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Australia's laws came into effect in December last year, with countries like Spain, India, Denmark, Norway, Malaysia and the UK announcing similar intentions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is time for Singapore to take clearer scientifically informed interventions to address these concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This should include setting up a Select Committee to study whether a ban is appropriate in par in parallel to the Government's ongoing study and engagement with counterparts.

sections.label: National AI Council representation
sections.summary: The new National AI Council must include representatives from societal sectors at high risk of adverse AI effects, not only industrial AI Missions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, at the top level, the new National AI Council must include representatives from the societal sectors that are at high risk for adverse effects from AI, rather than only boosting adoption via industrial AI Missions.

sections.label: MOE AI frameworks study
sections.summary: MOE frameworks exist, but a MIT Media Lab study found over reliance on AI may reduce functional brain connectivity and memory recall.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While various MOE frameworks are in place, a study last year by MIT Media Lab found that over reliance on AI may reduce functional brain connectivity and memory recall.

sections.label: Protected nature areas boundaries
sections.summary: The Government should establish clear legal boundaries for protected nature areas and protect remaining habitats key for planetary and societal health.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As called for in a 2024 Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan, the Government should establish clear legal boundaries for protected nature areas and protect the few remaining habitats that we have, which are absolutely key for both planetary and societal health.

sections.label: Southeast Asia per capita ranking
sections.summary: In 2024, Singapore is second in Southeast Asia per capita at about US$22,000, behind Brunei and ahead of Malaysia, Thailand and the regional average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In Southeast Asia, on a per capita basis, we are number two in 2024, at about US$22,000 per capita, behind Brunei.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We are ahead of Malaysia which is about US$10,000; Thailand, about US$5,500; and the Southeast Asia average of about US$3,500 and we are close to the OECD average of about US$23,000.

sections.label: OECD spending comparison
sections.summary: Within the OECD, Singapore is just behind US and UK spending and ahead of Korea and Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Within the OECD, Singapore is just behind the spending of US, which is about US$26,000; and the UK, which is about US$24,000; and ahead of Korea and Japan, both at about US$19,000.

sections.label: Retraining, fitness, CPF increases
sections.summary: The Government must do three things: compulsory retraining and skill upgrade every 10 years, staying physically and mentally fit to work, and increasing CPF contribution rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Government must keep our people fit to work, acquire relevant skills and grow their retirement nest egg.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: So, we need to do three things: one, compulsory retraining and skill upgrade every 10 years; two, staying physically and mentally fit to work; and three, increase forced savings rate or CPF contribution rates.

sections.label: Retraining funding and collaboration
sections.summary: MOM, MTI and MOE should collaborate to close gaps between industry needs, job projections and retraining courses, and the Government should consider funding retraining for workers at 40, 50 and 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: MOM, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and MOE must collaborate more closely to close the gap between industry needs in high-growth sectors, jobs projections and retraining or re-education courses, for example in sustainability, healthcare and information technology (IT).

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I ask for the Government to consider funding workers for retraining or reskilling for every worker reaching 40, 50 and 60 for six months.

sections.label: Healthy SG for aged 40
sections.summary: We ought to press on with Healthy SG for those aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, we ought to press on with Healthy SG for those aged 40 and above.

sections.label: CPF contribution and interest rates
sections.summary: With more Ordinary Account funds used for property, higher CPF contribution rates may need consideration, and the CPF Board could consider raising Ordinary Account and Special Account interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, with more use of the funds in the Ordinary Account for property purchases, we may need to consider higher CPF contribution rate from employer and employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Second, can the CPF Board consider increasing the interest rate of 2.8% for the Ordinary Account and 4% for the Special Account?

sections.label: Workforce strategy fundamental review
sections.summary: A fundamental review of workforce strategy is urgently needed, including mandatory retraining every 10 years, aligning education with job market requirements, and Government co-financing of retraining programmes amid rapid technological change and AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: A fundamental review of workforce strategy is urgently needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: This includes implementing mandatory retraining every 10 years, aligning the education system with job market requirements as well as co-financing of retraining programmes by the Government to maintain workforce employability amid rapid technological change, particularly in the era of AI. : Mr Speaker, there are two sides to this issue and changes need to be made both on an individual level and the Government level.

sections.label: Institutionalising retraining and lifelong work
sections.summary: Retraining arrangements should be institutionalised, such as training every 10 years, with closer alignment between education and market demands and Government subsidies, and Singaporeans should view work as a lifelong meaningful endeavour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Every employee is an important link in the chain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We should seriously consider institutionalising retraining arrangement, for example, allowing an employee to undergo training every 10 years, promoting closer alignment between the education system and market demands with appropriate Government subsidies to establish a more comprehensive retraining system, thereby maintaining employees' employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I also encourage Singaporeans to view work as a lifelong meaningful endeavour rather than merely as a means to retire early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I also advocate for continuous skills upgrading and regarding health as a key asset, so as to ensure our employability and competitiveness in the long term. : Mr Speaker, there is great urgency and courage required of us to carry out this revamp.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Urgency because otherwise, the young seniors will become a "lost generation", which the Singapore Government will need to support for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: No amount of CDC vouchers and subsidies would help us tackle this problem.

sections.label: Political will to transform discontent
sections.summary: We should find the political will, courage and urgency to transform discontent into hope and ability to remake our country and people for challenges ahead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Let us find within us the political will, the courage and the great urgency to transform discontent into hope and ability to remake our country and our people to meet the challenges ahead.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger
sections.summary: SSG and WSG will merge into one agency, jointly overseen by MOM and MOE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SSG and WSG will merge into a single agency, jointly overseen by MOM and MOE.

sections.label: SSG training participation 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, 606,000 individuals participated in SSG-supported training and 123,000 enrolled in courses with direct employability outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, 606,000 individuals participated in SSG-supported training, and 123,000 enrolled in courses with direct employability outcomes.

sections.label: Retrenchments rise in 2025
sections.summary: Retrenchments rose to 14,400 in 2025 amid a choppy global outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Retrenchments rose to 14,400 in 2025, on the back of a choppy global outlook.

sections.label: Permanent and fixed term employment
sections.summary: Over 90% of resident employees are in permanent jobs, around 7% are on fixed term contracts, and older workers are disproportionately represented among one-year contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the share declined slightly in 2025, with over 90% of resident employees now in permanent jobs, around 7% remain on fixed term contracts and older workers are disproportionately represented among one-year contracts.

sections.label: Working beyond official hours
sections.summary: Surveys show over 90% of employees worked beyond official hours and 71% feared negative repercussions for not responding after hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Surveys show over 90% of employees have worked beyond official hours, with 71% fearing negative repercussions if they do not respond after hours.

sections.label: CPF contribution and investment changes
sections.summary: Planned CPF contribution increases for senior workers proceed from January 2027 with a transition offset, and CPF will pilot a simplified low cost life-cycle investment scheme by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next step of planned CPF contribution increases for senior workers will proceed from January 2027, with a transition offset to help employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CPF will also pilot a new simplified, low cost, life-cycle investment scheme by 2028 to give members more diversified options above the base interest rates.

sections.label: Older workers want to work
sections.summary: NTUC's survey showed older workers are strongly willing to remain economically active beyond retirement and re-employment ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTUC's own survey showed strong willingness among older workers to remain economically active beyond the current retirement and even re-employment ages.

sections.label: Union training leave agreements
sections.summary: Negotiated training leave in collective agreements must spread to non-union and SME settings with redesigned shifts and modular courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where unions are present, we have negotiated training leave into collective agreements; this must be spread by example into non-union and SME settings, with redesigned shifts, modular stackable courses and just-in-time learning aligned to job redesign.

sections.label: Budget 2026 family support
sections.summary: Families will receive cash Cost-of-Living Special Payments, enhanced U-Save rebates and CDC vouchers for all households in January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Families will still feel Budget 2026's tangible support: cash Cost-of-Living Special Payments, enhanced U-Save rebates and CDC vouchers for all households in January 2027.

sections.label: Three Cs Budget debate
sections.summary: The speaker will contribute three Cs to the 2026 Budget debate: cost of living, caring for families, and core of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Today, I will contribute "3Cs" to our 2026 Budget debate – Cost of living; Caring for families; and Core of our Workforce.

sections.label: Question on surplus support
sections.summary: Some sought clarification on why a healthy surplus of 1.9% of GDP has not already translated to more support measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Some sought clarification – why a healthy surplus to the tune of 1.9% of GDP has not already translated to more support measures.

sections.label: Reviewing revenue measures timing
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider re-timing or reviewing planned revenue-generating measures or taxes in coming years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: My question is, would the Government consider re-timing or reviewing planned revenue generating measures or taxes in the next few years, especially ones which may directly lead to alleviating cost-of-living pressures?

sections.label: Preschool and student care subsidies
sections.summary: Raising the monthly household income threshold to $15,000 for preschool subsidies and to $6,500 for Student Care Fee Assistance extends help to more households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The upwards review of monthly household income threshold to $15,000 for preschool subsidies means help reaches more lower- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, the household income revision for Student Care Fee Assistance to $6,500 enhances access to after-school care, where students get the guidance they need and working parents get the support they deserve.

sections.label: Support for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The MP welcomes the announcement that strengthening support for persons with disabilities is a key Government priority and awaits task force recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, I welcome Prime Minister Wong's announcement that strengthening support for persons with disabilities is a key priority of the Government and I look forward to the recommendations from the task force that will be reviewing how Singapore can provide more meaningful support at different life stages for persons with disabilities and their families.

sections.label: ComLink+ social mobility programme
sections.summary: ComLink+ will see an additional $500 payout for families working towards milestone goals, and the Government should share interim findings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: One of Singapore's efforts to tackle social mobility is the ComLink+ programme, which will see an additional $500 payout for families working towards their milestone goals in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the scheme was first launched in 2023 it is timely for the Government to share meaningful interim findings on how ComLink+ is beginning to translate into better educational and social outcomes for the children.

sections.label: Residents' rising cost of living concerns
sections.summary: Residents of Fengshan, East Coast and throughout Singapore shared concerns about challenges from rising costs of living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Although Budget 2026 focuses on the long term to ensure a strong future, many residents of Fengshan and, indeed, East Coast as well as throughout Singapore whom I have met, shared their concerns about the challenges they face in dealing with rising costs of living.

sections.label: AI, workers and CPF contributions
sections.summary: The MP welcomes Budget initiatives for workers to use AI, asks about safeguards and sector-specific toolkits, and raises CPF contribution increases for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Budget also highlights initiatives to help workers leverage AI to automate routine tasks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the move and ask how the Government plans to assess how AI complements human intelligence, HI, and not replace critical thought at work and in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: What safeguards are in place to ensure AI does not inadvertently replace individuals or widen skill and income gaps in the workforce?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government could consider collaborating with various key industries to create sector-specific AI toolkits, so talents can effectively conquer AI in their domains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Government should prioritise ethics and governance in the AI agenda, because only then we can build a strong and resilient workforce that is skilled in using AI competitively and responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the young seniors, the planned increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers in 2027 is helpful for retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: But this must come with guardrails and capital preservation at the front and center.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, for older seniors who may face re-employment difficulties or are medically unfit, how will the Government support meaning contributions to their CPF accounts, so that the policy achieves its intended effect?

sections.label: Protections for platform workers
sections.summary: In the last term, protections for platform workers were strengthened, progressive wages advanced, and Flexible Work Arrangements made a legitimate workplace conversation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In the last term, we strengthened protections for platform workers, advanced progressive wages and made Flexible Work Arrangements a legitimate workplace conversation.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangement requests
sections.summary: Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests have been in place over a year, yet NTUC surveys show more than half of workers never made a request.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests have been in place for more than a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet in our NTUC Women and Families surveys, more than half of workers have never made a request.

sections.label: Childcare hours for shift workers
sections.summary: Childcare operating hours must reflect workforce realities, so the speaker calls for expanded flexible and extended childcare, including weekend and after-hours pilots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Childcare operating hours, especially in estates with shift workers, must better reflect workforce realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore call for support to expand flexible and extended childcare options, including weekend and after-hours pilots in selected communities.

sections.label: NTUC workplace inclusivity calls

sections.summary: The speaker supports the raised ceilings but notes they start January 2027, lists three asks on review, ComLink+ coverage and an April 2026 start, and cites falling marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Raising the income ceiling for preschool subsidies from $12,000 to $15,000 and the student care fee assistance ceiling from $4,500 to $6,500 are appropriate steps and I fully support them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A family earning $13,500 per month, which is above the current subsidy ceiling but below the new ceiling, still has to bear higher costs for another nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Every family the Government has acknowledged as deserving support through fee cap reduction, through expanded subsidy thresholds and through ComLink+ design, should receive that support well with predictability, without arbitrary age cut-offs, without a nine-month gap between announcement and delivery, and not only if they happen to be among the 10,000 families with a coach already assigned to them, The three asks I have made today are specific and proportionate, a published review of whether the structure of support for families with post-primary school age children is well matched to the cost they actually bear; a stated coverage target and coach investment plan for ComLink+; and for the last point, an explanation on why April 2026 is not feasible as a start date, and if the gap cannot be closed, a transitional bridging measure from families who are caught waiting using instruments that the Government has deployed before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the areas of Employment and Employability, FA4 can continue to strengthen relations with employers and industry partners, so that more training opportunities, internships and job placements are created in the growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On NTUC's part, through initiatives, like AI-Ready SG, we will continue to support workers and entrepreneurs in facing this change.

sections.label: Three transition foundations
sections.summary: The speaker says strengthening clarity, early trusted engagement and confidence will make transitions strengthen the workforce, citing OECD PISA and World Bank rankings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we use it wisely, this change is not a threat.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is an opportunity for our community to continue progressing confidently. : Sir, in closing, as transitions become more frequent in the age of AI, our responsibility is clear.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must strengthen clarity, so workers see the real pathways forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must deepen early, trusted engagement, so no one feels blindsided by change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And we must intentionally build confidence so that workers are equipped not only with skills but also with the self-assurance and resilience to move forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we get these three foundations right, transition will not weaken our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It will only strengthen it and Singapore will continue to move ahead with our workers, not ahead of them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Our most recent ranking in the OECD PISA has us ranked first worldwide and the World Bank's Human Capital Index likewise has put us up top.

sections.label: Schooling years and economic progress
sections.summary: Years of schooling rose from under four in 1960 to over 12 by 2015, with science and technical emphasis and sorting, making public education the backbone of economic progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The overall number of years of schooling in the population went from less than four years in 1960 to more than 12 by 2015, with an emphasis on science and technical education, coupled with a rigorous system of sorting and tracking, public education became the backbone of our nation's remarkable economic progress.

sections.label: AI eroding schooling edge
sections.summary: The advent of AI will mean an erosion of the edge in knowledge and ability that the schooling system previously conferred.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The advent of AI will mean an erosion of the edge in knowledge and ability that our schooling system had previously been able to confer.

sections.label: Large primary school classes
sections.summary: In primary schools, there are still classrooms with as many as 40 students.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In primary schools, we still have classrooms that have as many as 40 students.

sections.label: Children learn best from humans
sections.summary: Cognitive science research concludes unambiguously that children respond best to instruction delivered by another human rather than a device.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: While some champions of technology have lauded the promise of AI to produce education customised to each learner, research in the cognitive sciences is unambiguous in concluding that children simply respond best to instruction delivered by another human rather than a device.

sections.label: Examination weight and abolished mid-years
sections.summary: Mid-year and final examinations could comprise as much as four-fifths of the total grade, and abolishing mid-year examinations without rebalancing assessment weights keeps the effort half-hearted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Until recently, mid-year and final examinations could comprise as much as four-fifths of the total grade, which places an inordinate emphasis on these markers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, even though the Ministry formally abolished mid-year examinations three years ago without an accompanying rebalancing of the weight placed on examinations and tests versus other forms of assessment, the effort will always remain half-hearted.

sections.label: PSLE and O level tracking
sections.summary: The PSLE and "O" level examination remain major consequential tools for tracking students.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Furthermore, the PSLE and "O" level examination remain major consequential tools for tracking students.

sections.label: Frequent low-stake quizzes
sections.summary: Frequent but low-stake quizzes, as much as once a day, can improve conceptual retention and understanding.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Frequent but low-stake quizzes, as much as once a day, can improve conceptual retention and understanding.

sections.label: Early tracking and inequality
sections.summary: Evidence suggests early tracking between ages 10 and 12 increases educational inequality without clear achievement gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Similarly, the evidence on tracking too early, by early, the literature suggests between the ages of 10 and 12, which incidentally, is precisely when we start subject-based banding and institute the PSLE, actually increases educational inequality without any clear achievement gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: While Ministry officials had assured that subject-based banding, retain mixed form classes and which is consistent with research that supports how within school tracking can help students with heterogeneous ability actually cope better and promote positive peer influence, there nevertheless remains significant sorting between schools, which can undermine the benefits of tracking in the first place, while continuing to place undue importance of exams as a sorting tool.

sections.label: GenAI and graduate hiring
sections.summary: GenAI and Agent AI can do work new graduates used to fill, weakening firms' incentive to hire them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: GenAI can easily synthesise and deliver information that all but the very best undergraduates struggle to absorb, relieving the need for entry level positions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Agent AI can already accurately execute a wide range of tasks that new graduates used to fill, which means that firms will have a far weaker incentive for hiring them.

sections.label: Youth unemployment trend
sections.summary: Youth unemployment remains below other advanced economies but has steadily trended up since mid-2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Notably, while our youth unemployment rate remains considerably below those of other advanced economies, this has steadily trended up since the middle of 2024.

sections.label: University entry approach
sections.summary: Students must want to understand what they are taught, and the high-stakes university entry approach must be revisited.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Students must want to understand what they are being taught, not just cram yet more information without care for the fundamentals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: It also means that our outdated approach to university entry, which is conditional on relative performance in an academically oriented high stakes exam has to be revisited.

sections.label: Research funding plan
sections.summary: PM Wong's $37 billion Research, Innovation and Enterprise funding is welcome, though national R&D spending still lacks comparable economies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Prime Minister Wong's $37 billion funding for the Research, Innovation and Enterprise plan is undeniably a welcome step, and if resource constraints were the only limitation to research success, we would be well positioned, even though, as I previously mentioned, our national research and development spending still lacks those of comparable technologically forward economies.

sections.label: AI, diversity and education
sections.summary: AI compresses the talent gap and devalues traditional degrees, giving weaker students and those with undervalued skills a chance, and Singapore should embrace neurological and intellectual diversity in education.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Weaker students now have a more realistic chance than ever before to shine in the classroom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Not only will AI compress the talent gap, it will devalue the traditional degree, which opens the door for those who, endowed with hitherto undervalued skills, to finally stake their place in the modern economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This includes those who may not be as book smart, but who are gifted in myriad other ways.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Singapore has, since birth, been an ethnically, culturally and religiously diverse nation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Let us also embrace neurological and intellectual diversity, starting from the ground up with our educational system.

sections.label: AI, seniors and retirement ages
sections.summary: AI finds answers faster but experience helps Singapore ask better questions, and as a super aged society it aims to support seniors to age with dignity, security and peace of mind, with retirement and re-employment ages on track to reach 65 and 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: My argument is a simple one – that AI helps us find answers much faster, but it is experience in AI number 2 that helps Singapore ask better questions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As Singapore becomes a super aged society, our goal is to support our seniors to age with dignity, with security and with a peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)

sentences.text: NTUC’s Senior Employment Survey shows that more than 70% of senior workers are open to employment beyond the retirement age.

sentences.text: At Schneider Electric, for example, the Senior Talent Programme offers different “personas”, one of which is the “Pivot” persona, which enables senior workers to take on roles such as coaches and mentors while remaining engaged in the organisation.
