sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup is studying whether additional support can be extended to long-term unemployed seniors seeking to re-enter the workforce.

sections.label: NTUC AI-Ready SG initiative
sections.summary: NTUC launched AI-Ready SG, a one-stop platform for training, upskilling, firm transformation and job matching, plus AIRI, an AI Transformation Blueprint and sectoral AI Playbooks.

sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, NTUC has launched the AI-Ready SG initiative, which is a one-stop platform to train and upskill workers, support firms in transformation and improve matching for workers to access better jobs.

Apart from the support given to workers in areas such as training and matching, NTUC has actually launched for quite some time an AI Readiness Index (AIRI), which I think Member Denise Phua will be happy to know, an AI Transformation Blueprint and more recently, sectoral AI Playbooks that provide companies with practical guidance on business transformation and resources to support their workers' upskilling.

sections.summary: At Tan Tock Seng Hospital, an AI-enabled predictive patient monitoring system has helped nurses manage fall-risk patients more effectively.

sentences.text: At Tan Tock Seng Hospital, the introduction of an AI-enabled predictive patient monitoring system has helped our nurses manage fall-risk patients more effectively.

sections.summary: With slower workforce growth from an ageing population and falling TFR, the Government launched the Economic Strategy Review in August 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: And where we would have to do more with a slower growth in our workforce, given our ageing population and falling TFR.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: This is why the Government launched the Economic Strategy Review in August 2025, and I have had the privilege to lead the Committee on Entrepreneurship together with my co-chair, Minister of State Alvin Tan.

sentences.text: We can introduce another similar credit scheme for employers who take a chance on persons from other vulnerable and marginalised groups and offer them meaningful long-term employment.

sections.label: Youth mental health statistics
sections.summary: About one-third of youths aged 15 to 35 reported severe or extremely severe depression, anxiety or stress symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Singapore, about one-third of youths aged 15 to 35 reported severe or extremely severe symptoms of depression, anxiety or stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Students dealing with these conditions miss about 190 hours – or 24 days – of school annually and mental health struggles cut down school performance by 63%.

sections.label: Expand Culture Pass to children
sections.summary: The speaker proposes expanding the Culture Pass to cover every child, not only citizens aged 18 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A study by the Singapore Symphony Orchestra shows that just bringing students to attend a concert together resulted in significant improvement in their well-being and sense of social connection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose that we expand the Culture Pass to cover every child, rather than only applying it to citizens aged 18 and above.

sections.label: Bishan space for special needs
sections.summary: The speaker is working on initiatives in Bishan Community Club for those with special needs and for family bonding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: During the briefing, I learnt about how some parents keep their autistic children at home for fear of the social rejection they would encounter should their children go through a meltdown in public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am working on an initiative in Bishan Community Club to make it a comfortable and conducive space for those with special needs, so they know they are welcome at our events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We are doing this by setting aside calm corners, training volunteers to know how to engage such families and designing wayfinding features.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also started an initiative to promote bonding between parents, grandparents and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is an indoor space with loose parts free play, which is going to expand to serve children with special needs.

sections.label: Volunteer mother in rental flat
sections.summary: A volunteer is a young mother of an eight-year-old boy with hearing disabilities who lives with her family in a rental flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I found an answer in a volunteer in my community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: She is a young mother of an eight-year-old boy with hearing disabilities, and she lives with her family in a rental flat.

sections.label: Singapore investors in China
sections.summary: Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor for several years, with about 4,000 Singapore companies in Shanghai alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Despite our small domestic economy, Singapore has, for several years, been China's largest foreign investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In Shanghai alone, there are approximately 4,000 Singapore companies there.

sections.label: Singapore-China bilateral ties and CSFTA
sections.summary: Bilateral ties between Singapore and China have deepened, and the CSFTA lets most Singapore exports to China enter tariff-free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Over decades, bilateral ties between Singapore and China have deepened and expanded significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have a comprehensive China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (CSFTA) which allows the majority of our export to China to enter tariff-free.

sections.label: Johore zone and Singapore FTAs
sections.summary: The Government is pushing businesses to consider the Singapore-Johore Special Economic Zone, and Singapore has 28 implemental FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government is also pushing for businesses to consider stepping up at the Singapore-Johore Special Economic Zone, which is a natural and logical move, given our proximity, our familiarity, as well as our complementarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Singapore now has 28 implemental FTAs, including multilateral agreements, such as the ASEAN FTA, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.

sections.label: Anchor Fund and Financial Sector Fund
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund and $1.5 billion Financial Sector Development Fund announced in Budget 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Overseas expansions carry significant risks and often demand patient capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I welcome the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund and $1.5 billion Financial Sector Development Fund announced in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Budget surpluses question
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Singapore recorded a $15.1 billion surplus in FY2025 and a projected $8.5 billion surplus in FY2026 despite rising expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As the Budget debate is about financial policy of the Government, the elephant in the room question is of course how is it that despite rising expenditures over the years, Singapore recorded significant surplus of $15.1 billion in FY2025, with a projected $8.5 billion surplus in FY2026?

sections.label: Corporate income tax projections
sections.summary: Corporate income tax rose from $30.1 billion in FY2024 to $35.2 billion in FY2025 and is projected to reach $37.8 billion in FY2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Corporate income tax rose from $30.1 billion from FY2024 to $35.2 billion in FY2025 – the revised figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And it is projected to rise to $37.8 billion in FY2026, an increase of roughly one-third over three years, driven by stronger-than-expected growth and the implementation of the BEPS Pillar 2 top-up taxes.

sections.label: Public transport subsidy top-ups
sections.summary: A proposal for the Government to consider additional median-term top-ups to public transport subsidies beyond the baseline annual $2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And here I want to propose three areas for consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I will hope that the Government can consider additional median-term top-ups to public transport subsidies, beyond the baseline annual $2 billion to moderate fare increases.

sections.label: Taxing rich and foreigners
sections.summary: Lower- and middle-income families pay a GST rate of 7% or below, and the speaker asks why not tax more from the rich or foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Taken together, the lower- and the middle-income families effectively pays a GST rate that is 7% or below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I ask myself why would we not want to tax more from the rich or the foreigners who are here to spend more, and then use the financial resources to distribute it to the lower- and the middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is precisely because we remained in the position of physical strength that we are able to allocate meaningful resources across these three pillars: social development, economic growth and security in support of our long-term nation building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Prudent stewardship over the years has provided the Government with the capacity not only to respond to immediate challenges but also to invest strategically in our collective future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our strong fiscal position put us in good stead to confront emerging risks, seize new opportunities, safeguard Singapore's continued progress for generations to come.

sections.label: Benefits for children of unmarried parents
sections.summary: Children of unmarried parents do not receive the $11,000 Baby Bonus Cash Gift, family nucleus recognition, or the Parenthood Tax Rebate of up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One, their unmarried parent does not receive the Baby Bonus Cash Gift of $11,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Two, they are not recognised as part of a "family nucleus" for HDB schemes, they receive lower subsidies than the family grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Three, their unmarried parent is excluded from the most substantive tax benefits we provide for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They cannot claim the Parenthood Tax Rebate of up to $20,000.

sections.label: Non-working mothers childcare subsidies
sections.summary: Non-working mothers currently do not qualify for additional subsidies for childcare and after-school care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, non-working mothers do not qualify for the additional subsidies for childcare as well as after-school care.

sections.label: Subsidies for all students
sections.summary: The speaker proposes granting additional childcare and after-school care subsidies to all students and dropping the working mother criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us grant the additional subsidies for childcare and afterschool care to all students and drop the working mother criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Again, I do not believe that this will overnight make all of our working mothers wake up and decide to stop work, or this encourage those who are looking for work to not continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And this will include additional subsidy for the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children, subsidies for Special Student Care Centres, subsidies for children who need assistive technology and devices, like hearing aids.

sections.label: ASA process waiting time
sections.summary: The parents had spent more than one and a half years in the ASA process before coming to the speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the point where theycame to me, they had spent more than one and a half years since they started the ASA process.

sections.label: Adoption reassessment and leave
sections.summary: The speaker asks why another nine months and reassessment are needed, and notes adoption leave is 12 weeks versus 16 weeks maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Why the need to wait another nine more months to start the process, and why then the need to reassess them for adoption suitability, when things are going well with the first child?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And to compound the situation, compared to maternity leave of 16 weeks, adoption leave for parents is only 12 weeks.

sections.label: Streamlining adoption and subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker urges agencies to streamline the process, extend infant care, childcare and medical subsidies, and align adoption leave with maternity leave at 16 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, I urge all the relevant Government agencies and there are many involved in the process as I have described, to come together, work towards streamlining the process for parents significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And may I suggest that during the period where the child is in Singapore on a Dependent's Pass, let us extend the Singapore Citizenship subsidies for infant care, for childcare, for medicals to the child, because it is a matter of time that they will become a citizen, and these are critical developmental years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us not lose time and also let us align the adoption leave with maternity leave at 16 weeks.

sections.label: MOE exam achievement rates
sections.summary: MOE replied that at least nine in 10 students achieved AL6 or better in four PSLE subjects and about nine in 10 obtained C6 or better in three O-level subjects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MOE replied that for PSLE, at least nine in 10 students achieved AL6 or better in English, Mother Tongue, Math and Science; and for the "O" levels, about nine in 10 obtain a C6 or better in English, Mother Tongue and Math.

sections.label: PISA 2022 top performers
sections.summary: In PISA 2022, 41% of students were top performers in Math, 24% in Science and 23% in reading, compared with OECD figures of 9% and 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the latest PISA 2022 assessment of 15-year-olds, 41% of our students were classified as top performers for Math, 24% for Science, and 23% for reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In comparison, for the OECD, it was 9% classified top performers for Math, 7% each for Science and reading.

sections.label: National exam Math grades
sections.summary: The speaker says if 40% of the cohort are top Math performers globally, 40% should get the top or top two Math grades nationally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If 40% of our cohort are considered top performers in Math globally, then the performance on the national exams should reflect as such – 40% of the cohort should get the top or top two grades in Math.

sections.label: National exams, AI, student motivation
sections.summary: The speaker says national exams should assess competency, and that AI may harm foundational knowledge and cognitive skills, making motivation critical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The role of national exams should be to assess for competency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Foo, I am enjoying your speech, but you have a minute left.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: I believe this will be especially critical for generations to come with the advent of AI, because my concern is that the acquisition of foundational knowledge and fundamental cognitive skills will be impacted by growing up with AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Already, there have been studies that suggest that Gen Z may be the first generation that shows lower average intelligence quotient (IQ) and cognitive scores than previous generations for attention, memory and literacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: This is linked to screen time, digital devices and social media – and I have no doubt that AI will compound these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: In this context, it becomes even more critical that our students achieve fundamental competencies, and the most important factor for this is motivation.

sections.label: AI and cognitive development
sections.summary: The passage states that without this foundation, AI may only serve to retard cognitive development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Without this foundation, AI may only serve to retard the cognitive development instead.

sections.label: Singapore exports and higher duties
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gan noted that without secured exemptions, Singapore's exports from pharmaceuticals to semiconductors to advanced manufacturing could face higher duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Gan noted earlier this week, if exemptions are not secured, Singapore's exports, such as pharmaceuticals to semiconductors to advanced manufacturing, could face higher duties.

sections.label: India AI and data centre investments
sections.summary: India has announced ambitions to attract up to US$200 billion in AI and data centre investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: India has announced ambitions to attract up to US$200 billion in AI and data centre investments.

sections.label: Anchoring AI in strong sectors
sections.summary: Anchoring AI in strong sectors like advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics, financial services and healthcare creates higher value roles, resilient careers and stronger wage growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we anchor AI in sectors where we are strong, such as mentioned, as advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics, financial services and healthcare, and scale to more sectors with measurable outcomes, we create higher value roles, more resilient careers and stronger wage growth.

sections.label: Pooled AI engineers and modules
sections.summary: The passage proposes evolving CTO-as-a-service to AI-Capability-as-a-Service with pooled AI engineers for SMEs, and pooled industry resources for plug-and-play AI modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: First, evolve CTO-as-a-service towards AI-Capability-as-a-Service with pooled AI engineers deployed across SME clusters for hands-on implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Second, organise pooled resources by industry to co-develop plug-and-play AI modules with industry leaders for generic processes, such as quality control, logistics optimisation and predictive maintenance.

sections.label: Outcome-linked co-funding proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes outcome-linked co-funding tied to measurable productivity, cost savings, export growth or energy efficiency, noting many MPs shared this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Third, introduce outcome-linked co-funding tied to measurable productivity, cost savings, export growth or energy efficiency, something that was shared by many Members of Parliament yesterday.

sections.label: Income inequality and senior re-employment
sections.summary: It states the post-tax-and-transfer Gini fell from about 0.47 to around 0.37, real incomes at the 20th percentile grew faster than the median, and the re-employment age rises to 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Our post-tax-and-transfer Gini coefficient has fallen from about 0.47 in the mid-2000s to around 0.37 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Real incomes at the 20th percentile have grown faster than the median, supported by Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model and OECD studies indicate relatively strong intergenerational mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: For senior workers, the re-employment age will rise to 70 by 2030.

sections.label: Job redesign for seniors
sections.summary: It says seniors face challenging lived realities seeking employment aligned to their experience, and calls for accelerating structured job redesign using AI and automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But for our seniors looking for jobs, the lived realities remain challenging for them to seek employment aligned to their experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We must accelerate structured job redesign using AI and automation to reduce physical strain and enhance productivity.

sections.label: Wayfinding project and scaling pathways
sections.summary: It describes a trial with visually impaired residents using indoor positioning and AI image recognition, and asks about clearer pathways linking community innovators, GovTech, IMDA, healthcare institutions and social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Recently, I trialed a project with visually impaired residents to test a wayfinding solution using indoor positioning and AI image recognition to navigate complex indoor spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But how do we connect such projects to agencies, funding and testbeds and scale them with less friction?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We may need a clearer pathway linking community innovators, GovTech, IMDA, healthcare institutions and social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As digital adoption deepens, cybersecurity and scam prevention must keep pace.

sections.label: AI strategy for better lives
sections.summary: It states AI must strengthen industries, uplift SMEs, empower seniors, open doors for graduates and protect the vulnerable, translating into better lives and good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: AI must strengthen industries, uplift SMEs, empower seniors, open doors for graduates and protect the vulnerable, among many others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Above all, our strategy must translate into better lives and good jobs that are higher value, skills-based, fairly paid and future resilient.

sections.label: Support for ComLink+ enhancement
sections.summary: The passage states support for enhancing ComLink+, a scheme helping families progress from public rental towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, I support the enhancement of ComLink+, which is a scheme that helps families progress from public rental towards home ownership.

sections.label: PARF rebate reduction
sections.summary: PARF rebate reduced by 45% and cap lowered from $60,000 to $30,000 for COEs from February 2026 second bidding exercise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: As announced, the PARF rebate will be reduced by 45% and the cap lowered from $60,000 to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This change applies to Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) obtained from the second COE bidding exercise in February 2026 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: My concern is the effective date and the absence of transition safeguards for buyers who had already committed to a car purchase under the prior framework.

sections.label: Concerns on car policy change
sections.summary: Speaker asks about relief for buyers, impact on dealers, COE renewals, EV readiness, and trust when value is taken away.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Third, will the Government consider introducing a limited relief mechanism for buyers who entered into purchase agreements and paid deposits before Budget Day?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fourth, did the Government consider the impact on new-car sellers who typically commit to inventory and order pipelines six to 12 months in advance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For these new car dealers, they are now at risk of holding stock that is much harder to sell and may have a knock-out effect on their business viability and also employees' jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fifth, did the Government expect this change to increase COE renewals because retaining older cars becomes relatively more attractive and if so, what is the expected impact on the number of COEs available for the new cars and the resulting trajectory of the COE premiums?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For example, is the national power grid ready to support a mass adoption of EVs, and will EV charging, especially in older estates, keep in pace, so Singaporeans will not feel that policy is moving faster than practical realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But when the Government takes away value, it can be immediate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I worry this perception would erode trust, especially if ordinary families are hurt because they are not sophisticated buyers and reasonably expect the rules to remain stable when making big purchases.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: Government provides employers a Senior Employment Credit for seniors who wish to continue working, extended another year in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If seniors wish to continue working, the Government provides employers with a Senior Employment Credit, which has been extended for another year under this year's Budget.

sections.label: Seniors living alone 2030
sections.summary: Ministerial Committee on Ageing estimates 83,000 seniors above 65 will live alone by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Ministerial Committee on Ageing, an estimated 83,000 seniors above 65 years will live alone by the year 2030.

sections.label: Older adults below secondary education
sections.summary: Department of Statistics Population trends 2025 shows nearly 40% of those over 55 had below secondary education as at 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics Population trends 2025, as at 2024, nearly 40% of those over 55 years old, have education at below secondary level – a very significant segment.

sections.label: Hougang HDB branch closure
sections.summary: Hougang HDB Branch closed 1 September for an integrated project; counter services replaced by electronic and self-service machines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): The HDB Branch Office at Hougang Central closed on 1 September, affecting areas, including Hougang Single Member Constituency and parts of Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In response to the related issue raised in Parliament by Hougang Member of Parliament (MP) Dennis Tan, the Ministry of National Development responded that the Hougang Branch closed on 1 September to make way for the development of an integrated commercial and residential project in the vicinity of Hougang Avenue 10 and Hougang Central.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, HDB has not established a new physical branch nearby, but has replaced counter services with electronic service and self-service machines.

sections.label: Seniors' support and living arrangements
sections.summary: A wage-earning adult child living with parents may make seniors ineligible for support or reduce it compared to living alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should a wage-earning adult child decide to live with his or her parents for mutual support, the seniors may become ineligible for support or have support reduced compared to if they lived on their own.

sections.label: Per capita household income criterion
sections.summary: It asks whether the per capita household income criterion for schemes like Silver Support could be removed and seniors' own income used.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it be possible for instance, to do away with the per capita household income criterion for schemes, such as Silver Support, and simply look at the seniors' own income?

sections.label: Harmonised medical examination report scheme
sections.summary: Under the harmonised medical examination report scheme from 2 February, drivers attend one medical examination used by both agencies, with the doctor uploading the report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some have also had difficulties uploading the medical reports onto the portals of the two agencies, as they were not comfortable handling attachments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Now, under the new harmonised medical examination report scheme implemented on 2 February, drivers need only attend one medical examination that can be used by both agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, the doctor will be the one uploading the medical report onto the relevant portal.

sections.label: Fertility support recommendations
sections.summary: Citing infertility statistics and low total fertility rate, MPs propose fertility screenings, ART subsidies, higher MediSave limits and private clinic co-funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The struggles they face are deeply personal, often invisible and sometimes painful." SingHealth statistics indicate that roughly one in six couples, about 17%, experience infertility in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: FSS' community engagements reveal that financial costs are the top stressor, forcing some to abandon their fertility journey entirely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With two successive years of historically low TFR, Sir, the time to act is now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My fellow PAP Women's Wing MPs and I stand aligned with FSS' recommendations to propose several feasible solutions to create those "right conditions": one, promote early health screenings for fertility, potentially collaborating with the Registry of Marriages and as part of the Healthy SG movement; two, increased subsidies for assisted reproductive treatments (ART); three, raising the MediSave utilisation limit for ART and allowing treatments in private clinics to alleviate long waiting times in public hospitals where time is of the essence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Additionally, we recommend Government to co-fund for ART at private clinics, expanding MediSave withdrawals from three to six cycles, MediSave coverage for elective egg freezing, subsidised fertility screenings for couples and enhanced workplace support for fertility and family-building.

sections.label: Support for families and working mothers
sections.summary: It seeks priority for bigger HDB flats, flexible CDA use, and reinstated working mother tax incentives for career progression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As such, I hope that HDB can provide access to bigger HDB flats by granting priority as second timers to the Sale of Balance Flats for families with two or more children who wish to upgrade and live closer to or with their parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For children’s education, we must keep expenses affordable by offering better flexibility in tapping on the Child Development Account (CDA) funds for preschool-recommended enrichment lessons and field trips, for example.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We should also support continuous career progression for working parents, especially mothers, ensuring stable incomes to cover growing expenses for ageing parents and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I urge reinstating the working mother tax incentives to allow mothers who earned more income each year to claim a larger amount of tax relief for each child, so as to motivate mothers to remain and/or return to the workforce when they feel ready to pursue leadership positions.

sections.label: Frailty programme and LPA fees
sections.summary: It cites the Frailty Management Programme and suggests waiving LPA registration fees and revamping the Wills Registry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A recent example is the Frailty Management Programme that was launched in Care Corner Active Ageing Centres in Woodgrove and Marsiling, with a comprehensive and tailored care plan and close monitoring to address our seniors’ physical, nutritional and social needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But I believe more can be done to increase the take-up rates, especially among our seniors, such as: one, continuing to waive the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) registration fees for Singaporeans; and two, considering a revamp of the Wills Registry, while ensuring users are properly advised by legal professionals and better protected.

sections.label: AI strategy focuses on adoption
sections.summary: The speaker says the AI strategy's fiscal levers mainly target adoption, identifying where AI can improve existing industries and subsidising businesses to deploy it faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Right now, the heavy ﬁscal levers in our AI strategy are largely focused towards adoption – identifying where AI can improve our existing industries and subsidising our businesses to deploy it faster.

sections.label: Case for Edge AI niche
sections.summary: The speaker argues for another niche with global export potential: Edge AI and the efficiency research underpinning it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We must now look further aﬁeld with global ambitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I want to make the case for another niche, one with global export potential – Edge AI and the efﬁciency research that underpins it.

sections.label: Model distillation and quantisation
sections.summary: The speaker describes model distillation and quantisation as compressing large AI models to run locally with minimal performance loss, no cloud connection and a fraction of the energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This global problem, in other words, is the same problem our constraints have been forcing us to think about – how do you make AI run on less?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is the ﬁeld of model distillation and quantisation, compressing large AI models so they can run locally, with minimal degradation in performance, without an Internet connection to the cloud, on a fraction of the energy.

sections.label: Edge AI as RIE2030 priority
sections.summary: The speaker asks that within the $37 billion RIE2030 envelope, Edge AI efficiency research be named an explicit priority, with success measured by commercial export potential, not just domestic adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has already committed $37 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 (RIE2030) plan, with AI explicitly within the scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask that within that envelope, Edge AI efﬁciency research – model distillation, quantisation and on-device deployment – be named as an explicit priority, with success measured by commercial export potential and not just domestic adoption.

sections.label: Stanford and ADP hiring research
sections.summary: The speaker cites October research by Stanford University and ADP finding US entry-level hiring in AI-exposed sectors fell 16% since late 2022, and 20% for software developers aged 22 to 25.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Research published in October last year by Stanford University and ADP found that since late 2022, which was when ChatGPT broke cover, entry-level hiring in AI-exposed sectors in the US has fallen by 16%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For software developers aged 22 to 25 speciﬁcally, the headcount has fallen by a greater 20%.

sections.label: MOM granular employment data
sections.summary: The speaker calls on MOM to publish granular employment data for new graduates, broken down by sector, role type and AI exposure levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We cannot manage what we do not measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I call on MOM to publish granular employment data for new graduates, broken down by sector, role type and AI exposure levels.

sections.label: EIS deduction graduate roles
sections.summary: Requires firms claiming the EIS deduction above a threshold to show a credible plan for maintaining graduate and entry level roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While the details are being firmed up, I ask that the Government require that firms claiming the EIS deduction above a meaningful threshold demonstrate a credible plan for maintaining graduate and entry level roles, not by preserving roles that AI has genuinely made redundant, but by investing and reimagining what junior work looks like in an AI-augmented firm.

sections.label: Lowering qualifying age to 35
sections.summary: Lowering the qualifying age to 35 is a simple, concrete and targeted step addressing where the disruption is occurring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lowering the qualifying age to 35 is a simple, concrete and targeted step that addresses where the disruption is actually occurring.

sections.label: Without buffer, underemployment cycle
sections.summary: Without that buffer, the response to uncertainty is paralysis or taking the first job, causing underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Without that buffer, the rational response to uncertainty is not agility, it is paralysis or grabbing the first job that comes along, plunging workers into a cycle of underemployment.

sections.label: Targeted retraining tax credit
sections.summary: Proposes a targeted retraining tax credit only for firms that reskilled a specific worker into an AI-augmented role rather than retrenching them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: AI makes substitution easier than it has ever been.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I propose a targeted retraining tax credit, available only to firms that can demonstrate that they have reskilled a specific worker into an AI-augmented role rather than retrenching them.

sections.label: Annual AI gains audit
sections.summary: Proposes an annual AI gains audit scoped to four sectors to check whether productivity gains flow to workers' wages or shareholder returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These are the right priorities, but they come with a public obligation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I propose that an annual AI gains audit, scoped specifically to these four sectors, be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Not red tape for every business, but a targeted accountability mechanism for sectors receiving extraordinary levels of public support to answer one straightforward question: are the productivity gains from state-backed AI Missions flowing into the wages of our workers or are they flowing into shareholder returns?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Protect the worker that is being asked to adapt to it and ensure that the gains of AI accrue to workers and not capital owners.

sections.label: MOH operating expenditure
sections.summary: MOH's operating expenditure in this Budget is about $20 billion, and healthcare spending has more than doubled over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) operating expenditure is about $20 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, healthcare spending has more than doubled.

sections.label: Budget 2026 fiscal balance
sections.summary: Budget 2026 invests where necessary, strengthens fiscal structures and financing mechanisms, and keeps the system strong for this and the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 reflects that balance investing where necessary, strengthening fiscal structures and our financing mechanisms, and ensuring that our system remains strong not only for this generation, but for the next.

sections.label: Primary and community care
sections.summary: Embedding strong primary and community care early in all estates prevents avoidable strain as the population ages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Embedding strong primary and community care early in all estates is how we prevent avoidable strain as our population ages.

sections.label: Healthier SG and care capacity
sections.summary: Budget 2026 strengthens this direction through Healthier SG enrolment, primary care reinforcement, and expanded community and long-term care capacity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 strengthens this direction through Healthier SG enrolment, primary care reinforcement, and expanded community and long-term care capacity.

sections.label: Value from acute medicine
sections.summary: It ensures investment in acute medicine delivers full value, with shorter time-to-rehabilitation, stronger community therapy capacity and tracking of functional outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It ensures that our investment in acute medicine delivers full value.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can continue refining this by shortening time-to-rehabilitation after discharge, strengthening community therapy capacity and tracking functional outcomes to ensure quality and accountability.

sections.label: Elderly fear becoming burden
sections.summary: Tengah residents said many elderly fear becoming a burden to families; the speaker supports MediSave, subsidies and long-term care support and preventive healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In conversations with residents in Tengah, I found that what many elderly people fear most is not their own suffering, but becoming a burden to their families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support the Government's continued efforts in MediSave, subsidies and long-term care support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The best healthcare is not only about treating illness after it occurs, but about preventing disease, promoting early recovery and reducing avoidable hospital stays.

sections.label: Affordability access quality
sections.summary: Affordability, access and quality do not happen by accident.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Affordability, access and quality do not happen by accident.

sections.label: Managing healthcare responsibly
sections.summary: It states that every part of the equation must be managed responsibly for healthcare to remain strong for this and the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we want healthcare that remains strong for this generation and the next, then every part of the equation must be managed responsibly.

sections.label: Kampong Glam rent increases
sections.summary: It reports median rent in Kampong Glam rose 25% from 2023 to 2025, with spillover risks to heritage businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 12 January, a report by CNA revealed that between 2023 and 2025, the yearly median rent in Kampong Glam rose from $6.02 to $7.54 per square foot, translating to a 25% increase over two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During our Sitting earlier this month, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for National Development confirmed that a small proportion of tenants did face rental hikes of 25% or more in these two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He, however, said that this involved leases for shops in high footfall streets, such as Haji and Bali Lanes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: High rents in Haji and Bali Lanes can easily have a spillover effect on other adjacent streets, such as Arab Street, which houses some traditional textile retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The disappearance of heritage businesses in Kampong Glam will be an irreversible thinning of the precinct's place meaning.

sections.label: Heritage business licences proposal
sections.summary: It asks whether parameters could be amended, such as introducing heritage business licences, to keep heritage businesses viable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it not be possible to amend these parameters to ensure that heritage businesses can remain viable in the areas, such as introducing heritage business licences, specifically for historic districts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would offer businesses some measure of protection from open market competition, as well as prevent the over-commercialisation of a historic district.

sections.label: NAS records declassification
sections.summary: It states NAS made metadata of around 780,000 records public and 68,000 filed records were declassified, with automatic declassification planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2023, the then Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information mentioned that the NAS has made the metadata of around 780,000 records available to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Senior Minister of State's statement, it was also revealed that 68,000 filed records have been declassified and made accessible to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An automatic declassification process will make records generally available to the public by default instead of requiring interested Singaporeans and researchers to undertake an opaque approval process to gain access.

sections.label: Data centre energy and water
sections.summary: It states data centres used 7% of Singapore's energy in 2020 and describes the Green Data Centre Roadmap efficiency targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Locally, data centres accounted for 7% of Singapore's total energy usage in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, data centres also contribute to the urban heating of our island, because for every one megawatt of heat removed from data centres by the cooling systems, 1.2 megawatt of heat is ejected into the environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, resource and sustainability concerns prompted the Government to issue a moratorium on data centre construction in 2019, which has been lifted in phases since 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In May 2024, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) released the Green Data Centre Roadmap, which established energy and water efficiency targets for data centres for the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government is confident that we are not only on pace to meet these efficiency targets, but to also ensure that the data centres' energy and water consumption does not create upward pressure on the utility cost for households and small businesses.

sections.label: Changed world and growth
sections.summary: It states the presentation comes as the Prime Minister described a profoundly changed world, with growth expected to moderate to 2% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is presented at a moment when the Prime Minister has described a profoundly changed world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, growth is expected to moderate to between 2% and 4%.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary and PWCS
sections.summary: The Local Qualifying Salary will rise to $1,800, and the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme will be enhanced and extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Local Qualifying Salary will rise to $1,800.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Credit Scheme will be enhanced and extended.

sections.label: Preschool subsidies and ComLink+
sections.summary: Preschool subsidies will extend to families earning up to $15,000, and ComLink+ enhancements can provide around $10,000 annually for families with young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Preschool subsidies will extend to families earning up to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: ComLink+ enhancements can provide around $10,000 annually for families with young children.

sections.label: ESG reporting and nation-building
sections.summary: Corporate volunteering and social contribution metrics can be integrated into ESG reporting, and a 'we first' society must be cultivated intentionally with measurable unity and normalised contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Corporate volunteering and social contribution metrics can be integrated into environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting frameworks, encouraging deeper private-sector ownership of nation-building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A "we first" society must be cultivated intentionally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Unity must be measurable, participation must be meaningful and contribution must be normalised.

sections.label: Mirxes Hong Kong IPO
sections.summary: Mirxes IPO-ed on the HKEX, raising HK$1.09 billion with China-linked cornerstone investors, listing in Hong Kong because SGX has no equivalent pre-revenue biotech pathway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On that day, Mirxes, a microRNA cancer diagnostics biotech company incubated over many years of Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) research at Biopolis IPO-ed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEX), raising HK$1.09 billion with China-linked cornerstone investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mirxes listed in Hong Kong, not Singapore, because the Singapore Exchange (SGX) has no equivalent to the HKEX pathway for pre-revenue biotech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Its cornerstone investors were Chinese entities holding over 40% of the IPO.

sections.label: Weak commercialisation pipeline
sections.summary: The system does not produce a strong pipeline, as Mirxes being the only billion-dollar IPO after 30 years of investment indicates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the system does not produce a strong pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That Mirxes is the only billion-dollar IPO or commercially significant R&D company after 30 years of continual investment tells you something.

sections.label: Fragmented deep tech landscape
sections.summary: The landscape is so fragmented that no single entity has the mandate, capital concentration or authority for large fast bets, and the SG Growth Capital merger raises whether to consolidate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Each has a logic, but the aggregate effect is a landscape so fragmented that no single entity has the mandate, the capital concentration or the institutional authority to make the kind of large, decisive fast bets that define successful deep tech commercialisation elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The SG Growth Capital merger of SEEDS and EDBI is a step in the right direction, but the deeper question is whether we have the institutional courage to truly consolidate to give one to two entities the capital, the mandate and critically, the permission to fail, at scale, rather than spreading accountability so thin that no one is responsible for ecosystem outcomes.

sections.label: Bpifrance policy investment bank proposal
sections.summary: A 10-year assessment found Bpifrance backed 80% of funded French startups and two thirds of French venture capital funds, and the speaker proposes an equivalent policy investment bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Its 10-year assessment found that 80% of French startups that raised funds between 2013 and 2021 received Bpifrance support, and two thirds of French venture capital funds have Bpifrance as a limited partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Bpifrance deliberately accepts below market returns, targeting 7% annually rather than 10% plus to take risk that private investors will not, training a generation of entrepreneurs and building an ecosystem from scratch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe we need an equivalent policy investment bank – an institution outside the civil service, incentivised to take risk and freed from line-item accountability, staffed with ecosystem builders, not risk-averse civil servants.

sections.label: Deep tech visa proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a company-driven deep tech visa tied to the company's credentials rather than income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An 18-month engagement with a materials engineer or a combustion engine specialist can redefine a company's trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose a segmented approach: a company-driven deep tech visa, tied not to income, but the company's credentials.

sections.label: Israel, Taiwan, South Korea IP rules
sections.summary: Israel attaches binding conditions to public R&D funding, ITRI spun off TSMC in 1987, and South Korea designates over 70 National Core Technologies requiring prior approval for export or M&A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Law for the Encouragement of Industrial Research and Development, the Israel Innovation Authority attaches binding conditions to all public R&D funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: IP developed with public grants cannot be transferred outside Israel without explicit prior approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Industrial Technology Research Institute spun off Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company in 1987, by transferring fabs, equipment, technologies and 98 professionals to a new Taiwanese entity – with significant government ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Industrial Technology Protection Act, South Korea designates more than 70 technologies across 13 fields as National Core Technologies – semiconductors, displays, batteries – and requires prior approval for any export or merger and acquisitions involving these technologies.

sections.label: Offshore IP transfer approval law
sections.summary: The passage proposes legislating that IP developed with public R&D funding cannot be permanently transferred offshore without prior approval from a designated authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Legislate that IP developed with public R&D funding cannot be permanently transferred offshore without prior approval from a designated authority – enforceable domestically against Singapore-domiciled entities and individuals.

sections.label: Singapore integrated care efforts
sections.summary: The passage states that AIC, regional health systems, community care and Age Well SG show foresight, and that integration is underway through care coordinators and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The formation of the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), the development of regional health systems, expansion of community care and ageing in place initiatives, like the Age Well SG, demonstrate our strong foresight and the sustained effort by the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the whole of Government.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Integration is already underway through care coordinators, transitional care programmes and stronger partnerships across primary, acute and community care sectors.

sections.label: Manchester integrated neighbourhood care model
sections.summary: The speaker studied integrated care models including Manchester Local Care Organisation, where patients with complex needs were assigned a single case worker supported by a multidisciplinary team.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: During my public health training at the Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, I studied models of integrated care that left a lasting impression on me, including work from the Manchester Local Care Organisation in the United Kingdom, where integrated neighbourhood care has been implemented at scale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Patients with complex needs were assigned a single case worker, supported by a multidisciplinary team, which included doctors, nurses, social workers and other allied health professionals.

sections.label: Integration through regional health systems
sections.summary: Integration begins when help starts once the need is recognised, piloted progressively within regional health systems using Healthier SG networks, care coordinators, digital records and community partners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: True integration begins when help starts the moment the need for that help is recognised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This can be piloted progressively within our regional health systems, leveraging our Healthier SG networks, existing care coordinators, shared digital records, community partners, including our community health posts.

sections.label: Support measures at mosques
sections.summary: Three measures: enhancing training and resources for mosque officers and volunteers, placing social health coordination officers at mosques attended by seniors, and expanding senior programmes at mosques.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, enhancing training and resources for mosque officers and volunteers so that they can work more closely with the health and social services sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, placing social health coordination officers at mosques that are more frequently attended by senior citizens so that assistance can be better accessed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Third, expanding senior citizen programmes at mosques to include health talks, health screenings and counselling support.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and senior employment
sections.summary: Two steps: create more opportunities encouraging lifelong learning, and expand meaningful employment opportunities for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, we must create more opportunities that encourages lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, we must expand on meaningful employment opportunities for seniors.

sections.label: Life expectancy and senior support
sections.summary: Life expectancy rose to about 83.5 years, food, healthcare and transport costs rose about 60% to 80%, and the Government supplemented seniors with cash and voucher support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Our life expectancy in Singapore has risen over the years to about 83.5 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: During this 20-year period, if we use the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS’) goods and services inflation calculator, a basket of goods and services under the food, healthcare and transport categories which, in my view, are three categories that affect seniors significantly, increased approximately between 60% to 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Accordingly, the Government has over the years supplemented our seniors in retirement with cash and voucher support in various forms: CPF and MediSave top-ups, Silver Support and the Pioneer, Merdeka and Majulah Packages.

sections.label: One-person senior households doubled
sections.summary: Department of Statistics figures show one-person households for those aged 65 and above more than doubled from 2014 to 2024, rising from 42,100 to 87,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics, the number of one-person households for those aged 65 years and above has more than doubled from 2014 to 2024, rising from 42,100 to 87,200 households.

sections.label: Limits and lack of authority
sections.summary: They were limited in how far they could go, and no agency had the authority or power to intervene directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Yet they were limited as to how far they could go, and no agency had the authority and or the power to intervene directly.

sections.label: Public Guardian intervention powers
sections.summary: The Public Guardian cannot intervene directly when a senior lacking mental capacity has no viable deputy, and a review of the Mental Capacity Act is asked for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Currently, the Public Guardian can only supervise or investigate matters involving LPAs and or deputyships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Under certain circumstances, the Public Guardian may appoint suitable third parties, like social workers or medical care providers as professional deputies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Mental Capacity Act, however, does not empower the Public Guardian to intervene directly if a senior loses his or her mental capacity and has no viable person who can be appointed as a deputy to make decisions and manage matters on his or her behalf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This could result in vulnerable seniors failing to get the support or timely intervention they need, even with many willing helping hands in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I ask if the Government will consider reviewing the Mental Capacity Act and empowering the Public Guardian to intervene directly in such cases?

sections.label: Australia Aged Care Act 2024
sections.summary: Australia recently enacted the rights-based Aged Care Act 2024, in force 1 November 2025, focusing on empowering seniors in aged care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Interestingly, Australia also recently enacted the rights-based Aged Care Act 2024 which came into force on 1 November 2025 with a focus on empowering seniors to uphold their rights, needs and personal choices in their aged care.

sections.label: Value of unpaid caregiving
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates global unpaid care labour at roughly $11 trillion, and a 2024 Duke-NUS study values informal caregiving for seniors 75 and above at $1.28 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum estimates compensation of unpaid care labour globally to be in the tune of roughly $11 trillion – 9% of global GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Closer to home, a 2024 Duke-National University of Singapore (NUS) study revealed that informal caregiving for our seniors aged 75 and above is worth $1.28 billion annually, an equivalent to 11% of our total Government expenditure on healthcare, which is today's second after defence.

sections.label: Seniors-led tier in fund
sections.summary: A specific seniors-led tier within the SG Partnerships Fund is proposed, offering higher funding for ground-up initiatives led and participated by those above 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is heartening to see the expansion of the SG Partnerships Fund, but we can be bolder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I propose a specific seniors-led tier within this fund offering higher funding for ground-up initiatives led and participated by those above 60.

sections.label: Toa Payoh rental flats
sections.summary: Toa Payoh Central has 17 rental blocks, and a Parliamentary Question reply this week noted the median number of occupants in a two-room rental flat is four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Toa Payoh, we have 17 rental blocks in Toa Payoh Central.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I noted in a Parliamentary Question reply this week that the median number of occupants in a two-room rental flat is four.

sections.label: Income and wealth inequality
sections.summary: Income inequality is at its lowest on record, but wealth inequality has widened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our income inequality is at its lowest on record, but the more insidious wealth inequality has widened.

sections.label: Paid caregiving leave funding
sections.summary: With a $15.1 billion surplus, the fiscal capacity exists to fund paid parent or elder caregiving leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With a $15.1 billion surplus, we have the fiscal capacity to do exactly that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Caregivers often torn between being at work and the bedside, just as childcare leave supports the role of a parent, we must fund paid parent or elder caregiving leave.

sections.label: Upskilling foreign domestic workers
sections.summary: Foreign domestic workers are not required to have senior care qualifications, so upskilling in geriatric and palliative care should be subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While staff in senior care centres uphold basic care and nursing competencies, yet when those same seniors requiring specialised care return home at night and on weekends, we do not require our foreign domestic workers to have these similar qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We should subsidise upskilling specialised in geriatric and palliative care.

sections.label: Support for larger families
sections.summary: Direct tiered support for families with three or more children must increase to keep large families a strength rather than a debt driver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If demography is destiny, and families are bucking the trend to hold up our TFR, we must increase direct tiered support for families with three or more children to ensure that the invisible infrastructure of a large family remains a source of strength rather than a driver of household debt.

sections.label: Humans in AI care network
sections.summary: AI helps identify vulnerable groups, but every node in the care network must be filled by humans, not cold machine interaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What they "Mai lai" or do not want to come, is that kind of cold interaction that has only graphics on a machine, without human dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must be clear: AI is the "ladder" that helps us identify vulnerable groups, but every node in the care network must be filled by humans.

sections.label: Three questions on Singapore's future
sections.summary: Three questions are raised: securing economic success and jobs, easing cost pressures and enabling progress, and a fiscal strategy fit for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, how will we secure continued economic success and good jobs for Singaporeans in a changed world?

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, are we doing enough to ease cost pressures and ensure every Singaporean can progress?

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And third, is our fiscal strategy fit for the future, the challenges we face both now and in the future?

sections.label: Manufacturing share of GDP
sections.summary: Manufacturing has averaged about 20% of GDP over the last decade and declined from 14% in 2015 to about 12% today.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, the manufacturing sector has, on average, contributed about 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And it has declined – from 14% in 2015 to about 12% today.

sections.label: F&B and retail declines
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2024, these fell from 26% to 17% in F&B and from 30% to 26% in retail.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, they fell from 26% to 17% for the F&B sector; and from 30% to 26% for the retail sector.

sections.label: Progressive wages and foreign manpower
sections.summary: It states uplifting incomes and supporting businesses via the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, and that the Dependency Ratio Ceiling cannot be relaxed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is the right thing to do – to uplift incomes, strengthen dignity in work and narrow wage gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And at the same time, to support businesses through the transition, we introduced the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and, in this Budget, we are enhancing the Scheme and extending it for another two years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mr Mark Lee asked for more leeway for SMEs to hire foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We cannot relax the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC).

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Doing so will encourage excessive reliance on foreign manpower and weaken our Singaporean core.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we will consider calibrated ways to provide more flexibility, like expanding the sources from which businesses can hire Work Permit holders, for certain types of occupations where genuine shortages exist.

sections.label: AI tools and ASEAN expansion
sections.summary: With Government support, it is developing AI tools to analyse customer data and shopping behaviour, employs 150 people and plans ASEAN expansion.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And with Government support, it is developing AI tools to analyse customer data and shopping behaviour, so as to enable more personalised product recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And it now employs 150 people and is making plans to expand into ASEAN.

sections.label: Permanent employment and PMET vacancies
sections.summary: Permanent employees rose to nearly 91%, vacancies outnumber jobseekers, and over 40% of openings are entry-level PMET roles.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The proportion of permanent employees has risen to a record high of nearly 91%, with gains across most sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Vacancies continue to outnumber jobseekers and over 40% of openings are entry-level professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMET) roles, indicating still healthy demand for young graduates.

sections.label: No jobless growth assurance
sections.summary: It states the strategy is clear and that Singapore will not have jobless growth.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is our assurance and that is why our strategy going ahead is clear.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will not have jobless growth in Singapore.

sections.label: Inflation spike and Assurance Package
sections.summary: It rose to more than 6% in 2022 and came down to 0.9% last year, cushioned by over $10 billion through the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, it rose to more than 6% in 2022 and it has since come down to 0.9% last year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To cushion the spike, we provided more than $10 billion through the Assurance Package.

sections.label: Household income examples
sections.summary: A lower-income household with young children has about $5,000, and a retired elderly couple about $7,600.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A lower-income household with young children – about $5,000.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And a retired elderly couple – about $7,600.

sections.label: One-off measures budget share
sections.summary: About 5% of the overall Budget is for one-off measures in FY2025 and FY2026, with 95% for longer-term structural schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because the facts are only about 5% of our overall Budget is for one-off measures – that was so in FY2025 and it is so in FY2026.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The remaining 95%, the overwhelming share, is for longer-term and structural schemes.

sections.label: Retirees and income growth
sections.summary: Retirees face greater impact as they are not working, so more is provided for them; incomes rose faster than inflation over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: He highlighted the concerns among seniors and, indeed, one group that will face greater impact is retirees because they are not working and that is why we provide more for them in the Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But when we look at data at both the household and the individual worker levels – household and workers – in fact, incomes have risen faster than inflation over the past decade, across the entire income distribution.

sections.label: AV and PCHI indicators
sections.summary: AV and PCHI are practical and effective indicators.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: AV and PCHI are practical and effective indicators.
